jobs.title: Fuels IC&E Engineer
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

Job Summary

Kairos Power is seeking an Instrumentation, Controls and Electrical (IC&E) Engineer to support the design, development, implementation, and optimization of instrumentation, controls and automation systems for the Kairos Power Fuels program. In this role, you will perform IC&E engineering activities for prototype and production systems supporting TRISO fuel fabrication, including equipment and instrumentation selection, design integration, system implementation, commissioning, and troubleshooting.

Responsibilities

• Perform IC&E design and engineering activities for prototype and production systems supporting TRISO fuel fabrication.

• Implement and configure process automation solutions in coordination with process, mechanical and other engineering disciplines based on defined process requirements, control narratives and safety design requirements.

• Develop equipment and instrumentation specifications and select appropriate IC&E components, including instrumentation, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), variable frequency drives (VFDs), motors, controllers, and input/output (I/O) components, based on process, control and operational requirements.

• Develop and review IC&E engineering requirements, equipment and instrumentation lists, data sheets, and related technical documentation.

• Review and contribute to piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) and other process documentation to support the development and integration of IC&E designs.

• Interpret Cause-and-Effect (C&E) diagrams and translate defined control requirements into control sequences and associated IC&E implementation.

• Participate in design reviews to evaluate mechanical and process designs for IC&E integration and define cabling, instrumentation, electrical interface, and equipment-control requirements.

• Coordinate with CAD and other design personnel to develop cable routing and instrumentation and electrical interface requirements for process equipment and skid designs.

• Provide hands-on engineering support for the fabrication, assembly, installation, integration, and checkout of controls and instrumentation for assigned systems.

• Develop and support execution of commissioning plans, procedures, functional tests, and associated test documentation for instrumentation, controls and process equipment.

• Support checkout and verification of instrumentation and control system inputs, outputs, alarms, interlocks, control sequences, scaling, and calibration in accordance with approved design requirements.

• Interface with vendors and suppliers to support technical evaluation, selection, procurement, and integration of equipment and instrumentation.

• Collect, review and analyze system and operational data to identify opportunities to improve IC&E design, system performance, reliability, maintainability, safety, and operational efficiency.

• Troubleshoot process automation, instrumentation, controls, and equipment issues during fabrication, commissioning, startup, and operations and support development and implementation of appropriate technical solutions.

• Participate in process hazard analyses and design and operational safety reviews, including HAZOP and What-If analyses, as applicable.

• Prepare and review IC&E engineering reports and other technical documentation related to assigned systems and engineering activities.

• Collaborate with facility operations and engineering teams to implement, optimize and sustain TRISO fuel fabrication processes and associated automation and control systems.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Instrumentation Engineering, or a related engineering discipline; an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be considered.

• 4+ years of relevant experience in instrumentation, controls, electrical, process automation, or related engineering work in a chemical, pharmaceutical, industrial, manufacturing, or similar process environment.

• Experience developing or implementing instrumentation and control solutions for industrial or process equipment.

• Experience reading, interpreting and working with engineering documentation such as PFDs, P&IDs, equipment lists, instrumentation data sheets, control narratives, and Cause-and-Effect diagrams.

• Experience specifying or selecting instrumentation and controls equipment based on process and operational requirements.

• Experience supporting the installation, integration, testing, commissioning, or startup of instrumentation, controls, automation, or process equipment.

• Experience working with hazardous processes or chemicals and applying appropriate engineering and safety controls.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with Rockwell / Allen-Bradley platforms (Studio 5000, CompactLogix or ControlLogix), including Add-On Instruction development and version management is preferred.

• Experience with Ignition or a comparable modern SCADA platform is preferred.

• Experience with EtherNet/IP remote I/O and IO-Link device architectures is preferred.

• Experience in nuclear, radiological or other regulated manufacturing environments, including their documentation and traceability expectations is preferred.

• Experience with modular skid design, fabrication and field integration, and with process unit operations such as powder handling, thermal processing, coating, compaction, or solvent recovery is preferred.

• Exposure to TRISO fuel, advanced ceramics, graphite and carbon-based materials, or high-temperature process systems is preferred.

• Experience scripting or automating engineering tasks (for example, Python or VBA) to generate controls code, tag databases, or test documentation is preferred.

• Experience with 2D or 3D design software (AutoCAD, SolidWorks or equivalent) sufficient to produce and mark up fabrication and installation drawings is preferred.

• Familiarity with process hazard analysis methods and functional safety concepts is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

• Knowledge of instrumentation and process control principles, including measurement, control loops, alarms, interlocks, control sequencing, and basic process automation concepts.

• Knowledge of industrial controls equipment and components, including PLCs, VFDs, motors, controllers, I/O, process instrumentation, and associated electrical interfaces.

• Ability to apply instrumentation scaling and calibration principles during system design, checkout, commissioning, and troubleshooting.

• Ability to troubleshoot instrumentation, control and automation system issues using engineering documentation, system data, equipment information, and observed system performance.

• Ability to support functional testing and verification of instrumentation, controls and process equipment in accordance with approved design requirements and test procedures.

• Ability to analyze technical and operational data and use findings to support engineering decisions and system improvements.

• Ability to prepare clear and accurate engineering documentation, requirements, reports, plans, and test records.

• Ability to communicate technical information effectively and collaborate across engineering, operations, EHS, quality, and vendor or supplier teams.

• Ability to manage multiple engineering activities and priorities while maintaining accuracy, documentation quality and attention to technical requirements.

• Ability to apply established safety requirements and practices when working with process equipment, instrumentation, controls, and hazardous processes.

Physical Conditions

• Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, scissor lifts, articulated boom lifts and the like.

• Moving self in different positions to accomplish tasks in various environments including tight and confined spaces.

• Remaining in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods.

• Moving about to accomplish tasks or moving from one worksite to another.

• Adjusting, moving, transporting, installing, positioning, or removing objects up to 10 pounds in all directions.

• Communicating with others to exchange information.

Environmental Conditions

• General office environment.

• Noisy environments.

• Odors or fumes from chemicals or chemical reactions.

• Assessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned.

• High-concentration, demanding and fast-paced.

Safety and PPE

• Reading and interpreting hazardous warning signs.

• Reporting issues with equipment or unsafe conditions.

• Wearing proper PPE, to include face mask, face shields, gloves, safety footwear, and other PPE as required.

Travel

• Some travel may be required, up to 5%

Additional Requirements

• Seldom requires working weekends.

• Occasionally requires schedule flexibility.

• Seldom requires extended hours to support launch and critical project timelines .

• Onsite: #LI-Onsite

About our Benefits

We know that we have some of the most talented and dedicated employees, and we believe in rewarding them accordingly. If you work here, full-time employees (excludes interns) expect to have access to the benefits below:

• Competitive compensation packages

• Medical, dental and vision benefits for employees and their dependents

• Paid Vacation

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. We actively welcome people of different experiences, abilities, and perspectives.

This team occupies a distinctive, high-visibility position at the intersection of accounting expertise and credit analysis, partnering directly with analysts, external investors, and market participants to uphold the analytical integrity of S&P Global Ratings' credit opinions. It is a rare opportunity to operate at the forefront of accounting developments while shaping how they are understood across one of the world's leading credit rating organizations.

What You'll Do

Impact

In this role, you will serve as a trusted accounting expert within S&P Global Ratings, translating complex and emerging accounting standards into credit-relevant insights. Your work will directly shape how credit analysts interpret financial reporting developments — and how S&P communicates those views to investors, ratings advisors, and the broader market.

Responsibilities

• Advise credit analysts on new and emerging accounting matters with credit relevance — including structured capital, AI Hyperscaler financing, debt vs. equity treatment, supplier financing, and leases — providing training and upskilling to strengthen analytical capability across teams

• Engage with external investors, ratings advisors, and other market participants to communicate S&P's views on the potential credit impact of accounting and financial reporting developments

• Contribute to the development of S&P Ratings criteria and analytical models, ensuring accounting standards are accurately and consistently reflected in credit assessment frameworks

• Participate in credit rating committees and management meetings, providing accounting expertise to support well-informed rating decisions

• Research and analyze datasets from S&P Capital IQ and external platforms such as EDGAR, publishing research and commentary on accounting topics with credit relevance

• Monitor the activities of accounting standard-setters and regulators, translating emerging requirements into credit-relevant insights; contribute to ad hoc analytical initiatives including AI and data automation projects

Compensation/Benefits Information

S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $123,000 to $190,000 Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual's geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses, and certifications. In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan. This role is eligible to receive additional S&P Global benefits. For more information on the benefits we provide to our employees, please click here.

Required Skills and Experience

• An S&P Global employee at this level would typically have 4–10 years of relevant experience in professional accounting, preferably at a large ("Big 4") accounting firm. National Office, Accounting Advisory experience or work with Accounting Standard Setters is a plus.

• CPA or Chartered Accountant designation — required for this role given the nature of accounting advisory responsibilities and direct representation with external market participants

• Demonstrated technical accounting skills, with the ability to bridge accounting issues with their related credit risk and economic implications

• Proficiency in financial statement analysis and accounting standards, including U.S. GAAP and IFRS

• Strong verbal and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex accounting concepts clearly to both analytical and non-technical audiences

• Spanish: Preferred — Professional working proficiency (able to communicate clearly at work in everyday situations and write professional messages); Portuguese: Preferred — Professional working proficiency

Preferred or Helpful Experience

• General understanding of credit analysis and its application to financial reporting and accounting assessments

• Experience in the corporate and infrastructure sector and its specific accounting considerations

• Experience contributing to analytical research, criteria development, or engagement with regulatory or standard-setting bodies

• Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent required. A master's degree or professional certification (such as CFA) is highly valued. We welcome candidates from traditional finance disciplines as well as diverse academic backgrounds that support innovative and critical thinking.

The Team

Credit Ratings is an integral part of S&P Global's Global Ratings Services, bringing together a diverse group of more than 1,400 analysts across key financial centers worldwide. The Corporates Ratings practice delivers forward-looking credit insights on a wide range of corporate entities, producing independent rating opinions that markets and investors rely on to understand how evolving risks affect financial stability and credit performance. The team provides analytical coverage of corporate issuers across the Transportation, Automotive, Aerospace & Defense, and Engineering & Construction sectors, monitoring industry trends, evaluating company performance and credit risk, and contributing to the ongoing assessment and maintenance of credit ratings.

Responsibilities and Impact

Impact

This role plays a key part in delivering the independent, rigorous credit analysis that underpins S&P Global Ratings' trusted, decision-ready intelligence. The Senior Analyst leads analysis for an assigned corporate portfolio, synthesizing complex financial and market data into clear, committee-ready rating opinions. By integrating AI-enabled tools with deep analytical expertise, the role drives productivity, quality, and consistency across the credit process — contributing to analysis that informs investors, issuers, and market participants globally.

Responsibilities

Team Contribution & Capability Building

• Provide day-to-day coaching and guidance to Research Assistants and Rating Analysts, building capability in credit analysis, data discipline, and analytical tooling while reinforcing values-driven behaviors.
• Drive consistency and scalability by codifying standard work and promoting the disciplined adoption of shared analytical practices across the team.
• Strengthen AI-enabled productivity by developing reusable assets and proposing lightweight automations that free capacity for higher-value human analysis and relationship work.
• Partner with senior team members and Data and Engineering colleagues to identify, design, and scale AI and automation use cases with governance built in from the outset.

Core Analytical & Delivery

• Lead end-to-end execution for assigned credits, ensuring high-quality analysis and timely delivery with clear accountability across priorities.
• Own ongoing surveillance for an assigned portfolio, synthesizing performance data, market signals, and peer context into decision-useful insights with clear risk implications.
• Support the embedding of AI and automation tools into analytical workflows, applying structured validation and analytical judgment to maintain the integrity and reliability of conclusions.
• Prepare and review key analytical outputs — including model inputs, metrics, assumptions, and published reports — ensuring alignment with methodology, sector frameworks, and evidentiary standards.

Stakeholder & Market Engagement

• Engage with external parties alongside senior team members, communicating complex analysis clearly and with credibility.
• Craft client- and executive-ready narratives that translate data, research, and analysis into clear, actionable stories.
• Build trusted stakeholder relationships through collaborative, adaptable, and analytically confident delivery.

Risk Management and Operating

• Ensure adherence to methodology, confidentiality requirements, and data governance standards; escalate issues early with clear options and recommendations to protect analytical integrity.
• Embed responsible, governed AI use into day-to-day workflows, using only approved tools and data while protecting confidential information at all times.
• Support the design, testing, and rollout of controlled automation and AI-assisted workflows, contributing to guardrail definitions that distinguish what can be automated from what must remain human-led.

• Practical experience embedding AI tools, large language models (LLMs), or automation into analytical workflows to improve productivity and analytical insight.
• Proficiency in analytical tools, with a willingness to learn data and automation platforms that support AI-enabled workflows.

Job Description:

DePuy Synthes, the orthopedics business of Johnson & Johnson, is recruiting for a North America Transport Operations Lead (M1), preferably based in Raynham, with remote as an alternative location in North America.

Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate its Orthopedics business to establish a standalone orthopedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal and regulatory requirements. Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes, and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans.

Purpose of the Position

The North America Transport Operations Lead (M1) is a key member of the global supply chain function, responsible for operational management of the transportation network across the North America region, including importation from global sites in other regions.

The role ensures the reliable, cost-efficient, and fully compliant movement of products — from manufacturing sites and regional hubs into local distribution centers, hospitals, and distributors — while safeguarding adherence to customs and international trade regulations across all operating countries.

This is a single regional leadership position that brings together two closely related disciplines: how products physically move (transportation networks, carriers, logistics providers) and how they cross borders compliantly (customs, import/export, trade documentation). The role partners closely with regional and global stakeholders enable uninterrupted product flow, mitigate risk, and drive continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

• Drive value across North America through optimized regional transportation flows for both inbound freight (from manufacturing sites and global hubs to regional hubs, and from hubs to local affiliates and distributor warehouses).

• Manage relationships with third-party and fourth-party logistics providers (including global Control Tower partners) through performance metrics, strategic direction, and continuous improvement programs.

• Support further deployment, development and maturity of the Global control tower in the North America region

• Lead performance measurement of transport reliability through critical metrics aligned with regional Plan, Make, and Deliver operations teams; provide input into executive performance reviews.

• Deliver on annual cost improvement and productivity targets through operational improvements while protecting service, quality, reliability, and compliance.

• Translate regional inventory strategy and business requirements into innovative transportation solutions; support transportation set-up for manufacturing network changes and new product launches.

Cross-Functional Leadership

• Partner with regional and global supply chain, Trade Compliance operations, Quality, finance, and legal teams to enable compliant product movement and rapid issue resolution.

• Represent transportation in end-to-end supply chain forums, projects, and sales and operations planning discussions; drive process alignment and trade-off decisions.

• Actively collaborate with the regional Deliver lead, distribution operations, and demand & supply planning teams to optimize capacity planning, reliability, and adherence to service commitments.

• Support product launches, network changes, and supply chain transformations by assessing and managing transportation impacts.

Key Objectives / Metrics

• Transportation cost and continuous improvement savings delivery.

• Transportation reliability — manufacturing/hub to distribution center, and distribution center to customer.

• Logistics provider (Control Tower) performance against agreed service levels and value creation targets.

Qualifications

Education

• Bachelor's degree required (Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, International Trade, or related field).

• Master's degree or MBA preferred.

Required Experience and Skills

• 6–8 years of progressive experience in supply chain, transportation, trade compliance, logistics, or related operational roles, aligned with a manager-level position.

• Strong working knowledge of international trade, customs regulations, and import/export operations within North America.

• Solid expertise across core transportation, planning, and carrier / logistics-provider management, including familiarity with control-tower operating models.

• Excellent analytical skills and an affinity for numbers: ability to support budgeting, financial reconciliation, and identify cost-saving opportunities in transportation.

• Good understanding of the order-to-cash process and end-to-end supply chain mindset.

• Experience partnering with global stakeholders and operating within a matrixed, multinational organization.

• Proven ability to manage complex operational issues, assess risk, and drive compliant outcomes.

• Effective communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills across cultures and geographies.

Preferred Experience and Skills

• Experience in medical devices, pharmaceuticals, or other highly regulated industries.

• Familiarity with global trade systems, transportation management systems, enterprise resource planning platforms, and transport & trade visibility & automation tools.

• Demonstrated experience leading regional or global process standardization initiatives.

• Understanding of good distribution practice and a quality-first approach.

• Lean or continuous improvement certification is a plus.

• Demonstrated awareness of artificial intelligence concepts and responsible / ethical use, with experience generating effective prompts to boost productivity.

Other

• Language: English required; additional languages are a plus.

• Travel: Up to 25–30% regional and international travel.

Job Summary

Working within Waterfall or Agile frameworks, a Business Analyst will work with a variety of disciplined focused team members all working toward a common goal of delivering value with quality and scale. Responsible for collaborating with other Job Families such within Technology and across our business partners to deliver consistent, reliable technology solutions that leverage AEP's technology standards, architectures and best practices.  Independently performs advanced business and project analysis for any sized project.

Job Description

The IT Consultant Senior - Customer Experience Systems Strategy and Solutions is responsible for business relationship, portfolio strategy, product direction, customer and employee experience, opportunity analysis, prioritization, adoption, and value realization across the Customer Experience Systems portfolio. The role jointly manages the portfolio with the Customer Experience Systems Engineering Lead and represents Customer Operations throughout planning, design, implementation, measurement, and continuous improvement.

The position partners with Contact Center and Customer Operations leaders, Technology teams, and Gigawatt partners to identify and shape AI-enabled and other advantageous technical enhancements. The role protects the intended customer and employee experience, defines business outcomes and controls, and ensures solutions are adopted and deliver measurable value.

What you’ll do:

Essential Job Functions & Tasks

Strategic Leadership

• Develop and maintain the multi-year Customer Experience Systems strategy and product portfolio roadmap.
• Align investments with Customer Operations priorities, customer experience objectives, enterprise strategies, regulatory needs, and measurable outcomes.
• Anticipate customer, workforce, channel, operational, and technology trends and recommend strategic responses.
• Drive simplification, reuse, application rationalization, and coordinated planning across the portfolio.

Business and Operational Partnership

• Serve as a primary Technology relationship partner for Customer Operations and Contact Center leadership.
• Develop deep understanding of customer journeys, operating processes, employee workflows, performance measures, pain points, and emerging needs.
• Facilitate portfolio planning, demand intake, prioritization, funding, governance, and executive decision discussions.
• Translate business and operational challenges into clear opportunities, product strategies, requirements, and outcome measures.

Product, Experience, and Analysis Leadership

• Lead product discovery, customer journey analysis, employee workflow analysis, process design, experience requirements, use-case definition, and value hypotheses.
• Serve as a primary business and operations partner for the move from Genesys Engage to Genesys Cloud CX, keeping the migration tied to Customer Operations priorities and the intended customer and employee experience.
• Shape the order in which each line of business moves to Genesys Cloud CX, balancing operational readiness, call volume, regulatory commitments, and cutover risk.
• Lead the review of current routing, IVR, self-service, and agent workflows, and decide what to redesign, simplify, or retire rather than move as-is.
• Make sure business requirements, acceptance criteria, and success measures are defined for each migration wave, and lead business acceptance alongside Contact Center leadership.
• Establish product vision, scope, business requirements, acceptance criteria, business ownership, roadmaps, and success measures.
• Use customer feedback, employee insights, operational data, analytics, and research to guide product decisions.
• Balance customer value, employee experience, operational need, risk, regulatory commitments, technical debt, cost, and delivery capacity.

AI Solution Partnership and Lifecycle

• Shape customer and employee AI use cases and partner with Gigawatt teams that lead development of underlying AI solutions.
• Lead business participation in experimentation, proofs of concept, prompt and conversation-design requirements, user evaluation, and business acceptance.
• Partner in data and knowledge readiness, human review and escalation design, responsible-use assessments, output-quality monitoring, solution-performance monitoring, and ongoing tuning.
• Define adoption, process integration, business controls, expected outcomes, and criteria for expansion, redesign, replacement, or retirement.

Technology and Engineering Partnership

• Work with the Engineering Lead from discovery forward to incorporate technical feasibility, architecture, dependencies, risk, capacity, and lifecycle implications.
• Translate portfolio priorities into clear business objectives, product requirements, experience requirements, and measurable outcomes.
• Participate in solution options and design reviews to preserve business intent and customer and employee experience.
• Jointly manage dependencies and tradeoffs across Genesys, digital channels, customer platforms, data, integrations, infrastructure, and Gigawatt-enabled capabilities.

Adoption, Change, and Value Realization

• Assess impacts to customers, employees, processes, policies, controls, training, communications, and performance measures.
• Lead operational readiness, stakeholder engagement, pilot feedback, adoption planning, and business acceptance.
• Establish baselines and monitor customer satisfaction, effort, self-service, first-contact resolution, employee productivity, quality, adoption, efficiency, and financial value.
• Use outcomes and feedback to recommend tuning, expansion, redesign, replacement, consolidation, or retirement.

Decision Support and Cross-Functional Leadership

• Lead cross-functional teams through influence and create clarity around objectives, roles, decisions, dependencies, and accountability.
• Jointly develop decision-quality recommendations on priority, solution approach, sourcing, architecture, AI risk, readiness, funding, and resources.
• Identify and engage the senior leaders, control functions, platform owners, and subject-matter experts required for informed decisions.
• Communicate portfolio progress, value, risks, dependencies, and investment needs to Technology and operational leadership.

Qualifications

Required

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, business, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
• Eight or more years of progressive experience in technology, product management, business relationship management, customer experience, business analysis, or related discipline.
• Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives from discovery through implementation, adoption, measurement, and improvement.
• Experience developing product strategies, roadmaps, business cases, customer journeys, process designs, requirements, and value measures.
• Working knowledge of Contact Center operations and one or more Customer Experience Systems domains.
• Understanding of AI-enabled solutions, data and knowledge readiness, responsible use, human oversight, solution evaluation, and monitoring.
• Strong executive communication, facilitation, analytical, decision-support, change leadership, and influence skills.

Preferred

• Experience supporting a large-scale Contact Center or Customer Operations organization.
• Experience with Genesys or another enterprise CCaaS platform.
• Experience shaping customer-facing or employee-facing AI, automation, digital, analytics, or self-service solutions.
• Experience in a regulated industry, preferably electric utility or energy.
• Product, Agile, SAFe, PMP, ITIL, BRM, design-thinking, business-analysis, or change-management certification.

Leadership Competencies

• Business Partnership
• Customer Focus
• Product Leadership
• Experience Design
• Analytical Thinking
• Change Leadership
• Financial Acumen
• Executive Communication
• Collaboration and Influence
• Risk Management

Success Measures

• Trusted partnership with Customer Operations and Technology leadership
• A clear, integrated, feasible, and outcome-based Customer Experience Systems roadmap
• High-quality product discovery, experience design, prioritization, and executive recommendations
• Successful adoption and measurable value from AI-enabled and non-AI solutions
• Improved customer and employee experiences across channels and journeys

jobs.description:

Job Summary

Responsible for the technical architecture and engineering integrity of the Customer Experience Systems portfolio. Leads solution design, software and platform engineering, infrastructure, system integration, and technical resource planning. Ensures solutions are secure, scalable, reliable, supportable, and sustainable. Promotes architecture principles, engineering standards, and enterprise technology solutions that meet business needs and align with Customer Operations and enterprise strategies. Provides technical leadership across solution delivery, production readiness, reliability, and lifecycle management. Decisions are guided by policies, procedures, enterprise standards, business plans, and portfolio objectives.

Job Description

The IT Consultant Senior - Customer Experience Systems Engineering is responsible for technical strategy, architecture, system design, engineering direction, infrastructure, integration, technical-resource planning, technical execution, reliability, and lifecycle health across the Customer Experience Systems portfolio. The role jointly manages the portfolio with the Strategy and Solutions Lead and translates desired customer and operational outcomes into secure, scalable, resilient, observable, supportable, and maintainable solutions.

The role must have sufficient Contact Center and CCaaS expertise to learn quickly, evaluate designs and configurations, guide technical teams, diagnose complex issues, and roll up sleeves when appropriate. The position is not primarily a project manager, Scrum Master, platform administrator, or production-support coordinator.

What you’ll do:

Essential Job Functions & Tasks

Technical Strategy and Solution Architecture

• Define current-state, transition-state, and future-state architecture and the engineering roadmap for Customer Experience Systems.
• Translate product roadmaps into technical strategies, solution options, architecture decisions, integration approaches, infrastructure needs, and engineering plans.
• Lead technical discovery and assess feasibility, complexity, dependencies, constraints, risk, effort, capacity, and sequencing.
• Establish reusable patterns, engineering standards, nonfunctional requirements, and design-review practices.
• Evaluate tradeoffs among buy, build, configure, integrate, and reuse options.

Contact Center and Customer Platform Engineering

• Provide technical leadership for the move from Genesys Engage to Genesys Cloud CX, from current-state assessment through each migration wave, cutover, and stabilization.
• Define the target architecture for Genesys Cloud CX, including telephony and carrier connectivity, routing and IVR design, identity and access, security controls, and integrations with AEP customer and enterprise systems.
• Work with Genesys delivery teams and systems integrators to review designs, configurations, and test evidence, and protect AEP’s architecture standards and long-term supportability.
• Lead technical planning for migrating integrations, data flows, and contact center reporting, and look for ways to reduce custom code and point-to-point integrations along the way.
• Own technical readiness for each cutover, including performance, resilience, failover, rollback, and production support handoffs, so service to customers isn’t disrupted.
• Build internal Genesys Cloud CX skills across the team, cutting long-term reliance on vendors and preparing AEP to administer and improve the platform after migration.
• Provide technical leadership for Genesys CCaaS, IVR, conversational self-service, voice, digital channels, routing, workforce engagement, recording, quality, analytics, and agent experience.
• Guide technical optimization of mobile, web, customer information, CRM, case management, knowledge, identity, communications, payment, outage, analytics, and data capabilities.
• Evaluate native product features, enterprise platforms, and custom-development options before recommending solutions.
• Monitor platform roadmaps, releases, deprecations, capacity, availability, performance, resilience, and technical opportunities.

Application, Data, Integration, and Infrastructure Engineering

• Lead solution design across applications, services, APIs, events, integrations, data flows, cloud, networks, environments, identity, and infrastructure.
• Ensure clear interface contracts, error handling, security, observability, resilience, performance, recovery, and support ownership.
• Promote DevSecOps, automated testing, configuration and infrastructure automation, repeatable deployment, and technical documentation.
• Reduce brittle point-to-point integrations, duplicated services, unsupported components, and unnecessary customization.

AI Solution Engineering Partnership

• Work with Gigawatt partners that lead development of underlying AI solutions while representing Customer Experience Systems architecture, integration, infrastructure, security, performance, reliability, and lifecycle needs.
• Partner in experimentation, proofs of concept, prompt and conversation design, AI evaluation and testing, and data and knowledge readiness.
• Define APIs, events, data flows, identity, access, monitoring, traceability, human oversight, fallback, and operational handoffs.
• Monitor technical and output quality, solution performance, security, reliability, and scalability and support ongoing tuning, expansion, redesign, replacement, or retirement decisions.

Hands-On Technical Leadership and Resource Strategy

• Provide technical direction to developers, engineers, architects, infrastructure teams, data teams, vendors, and systems integrators.
• Determine the skills, capacity, environments, tooling, and sourcing needed and recommend how to bring in or staff the right technical resources.
• Review code, configurations, designs, test evidence, and technical documentation when appropriate.
• Build or guide prototypes, validate critical assumptions, and diagnose complex technical issues when hands-on involvement is needed.
• Challenge vendor recommendations and protect AEP architecture, engineering quality, supportability, and long-term value.

Engineering Execution and Readiness

• Convert portfolio priorities into architecture deliverables, engineering tasks, estimates, dependencies, milestones, and technical work plans.
• Lead design reviews, technical risk management, cross-team dependency resolution, and engineering-quality reviews.
• Ensure functional and nonfunctional requirements are addressed through appropriate testing and evidence.
• Lead technical-readiness recommendations covering security, performance, resilience, observability, deployment, rollback, recovery, supportability, and production readiness.

Reliability, Security, and Lifecycle Engineering

• Establish service objectives and measures for availability, performance, capacity, resilience, recoverability, observability, supportability, and maintainability.
• Lead engineering analysis of significant or recurring incidents and ensure root causes are addressed.
• Guide vulnerability remediation, problem management, obsolescence planning, technical debt reduction, platform lifecycle, and modernization.
• Ensure production teams have adequate telemetry, documentation, runbooks, escalation paths, and technical knowledge.
• Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, data governance, accessibility, records, and regulatory requirements from the beginning.

Decision Support and Cross-Functional Technical Leadership

• Jointly prepare decision-quality recommendations on solution approach, architecture, buy-build-configure-reuse choices, exceptions, AI risk, sourcing, funding, resources, and production readiness.
• Explain technical options, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, staffing, cost, sequencing, and lifecycle implications to senior technical and operational leaders.
• Identify and engage appropriate architecture, cybersecurity, infrastructure, data, legal, privacy, finance, procurement, governance, platform, and vendor stakeholders.
• Mentor technical resources and promote shared standards, internal knowledge, automation, and reduced vendor dependency.

Qualifications

Required

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, or a related technical field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
• Eight or more years of progressive experience in software development, application engineering, solution architecture, platform engineering, infrastructure, system integration, or a related discipline.
• Experience providing technical leadership for complex enterprise applications, platforms, integrations, infrastructure, or software-delivery initiatives.
• Strong understanding of architecture, software engineering, APIs, integration, data flows, cloud, infrastructure, security, testing, deployment, observability, reliability, and supportability.
• Experience translating product needs into technical options, architecture, plans, estimates, resource needs, and executable work.
• Demonstrated ability to review technical designs or configurations, guide prototypes, lead problem diagnosis, and roll up sleeves when appropriate.
• Experience leading through influence across internal teams, vendors, and systems integrators.

Preferred

• Experience supporting broad Customer Experience Systems or large-scale Contact Center and Customer Operations environments.
• Experience integrating customer-facing or employee-facing AI, automation, conversational, analytics, or digital capabilities.
• Experience with AWS, API management, identity, data platforms, observability, DevSecOps, resilience engineering, and cybersecurity controls.

The successful candidate can guide engineers and vendors, evaluate tradeoffs, secure the right technical resources, review configurations and designs, lead prototypes, and diagnose complex issues while maintaining focus on enterprise alignment and lifecycle sustainability.

• Help the Store Manager supervise, train, and develop Store Associates

• Responsible for maintaining the cleanliness throughout the store, including cleaning and restocking bathrooms, sweeping and mopping floors, taking out the trash, and ensuring all areas are neat and presentable

jobs.title: Sr FA Engineer
jobs.description:
At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe.

JOB SUMMARY

Direct Failure Analysis Engineers in operating within area of assigned responsibilities with a high level of efficiency, integrity and enthusiasm, striving to achieve excellence in all endeavors.  Responsible for investigating and reducing component failures at electrical test through prompt, aggressive root cause analysis and effective corrective actions.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

TECHNICAL MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES
·         Improve component quality of non-conforming products by establishing failure analysis and obtaining corrective action from suppliers.
·         Interact with various departments (Quality, Purchasing, Manufacturing) to resolve/improve component issues.
·         Monitor components reject levels and respond to issues accordingly.
·         Report technical information concerning component failures to various team members and customer.
·         Reclaim revenue of rejected components via return of defective product.
·         Implement proactive measures that will foster productivity and higher product yields while reducing economic loss.
·         Respond to production line part problems immediately and address boards on component hold.
·         Monitor the storage of moisture sensitive components in dry pack and nitrogen cases; shock sensitive devices.
·         Follow ESD procedures at all times.
·         Speak with customer engineering personnel in a professional and effective manner.
·         Adhere to all safety and health rules and regulations associated with this position and as directed by supervisor.
·         Comply and follow all procedures within the company security policy.

LEADERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES (if applicable)
Recruitment and Retention:
·         Recruit and interview Failure Analysis Engineers and Technicians.
·         Communicate criteria to recruiters for Failure Analysis Engineer and Technician position candidates.
·         Coach Failure Analysis Engineers in the interviewing/hiring process.
·         Monitor team member turnover; identify key factors that can be improved; make improvements.

Employee and Team Development:
·         Identify individual and team strengths and development needs on an ongoing basis.
·         Create and/or validate training curriculum in area of responsibility.
·         Coach and mentor Failure Analysis Engineering staff to deliver excellence to every internal and external customer.

Performance Management:
·         Establish clear measurable goals and objectives by which to determine individual and team results (i.e. operational metrics, results against project timelines, training documentation, attendance records, knowledge of operational roles and responsibilities, personal development goals).
·         Solicit ongoing feedback from Test Engineering Manager, Workcell Manager (WCM), Business Unit Manager (BUM), peers and team member on team member’s contribution to the Workcell team.  Provide ongoing coaching and counseling to team member based on feedback.
·         Express pride in staff and encourage them to feel good about their accomplishments.
·         Perform team member evaluations professionally and on time.
·         Drive individuals and the team to continuously improve in key operational metrics and the achievement of the organizational

goals.
·         Coordinate activities of large teams and keep them focused in times of crises.
·         Ensure recognition and rewards are managed fairly and consistently in area of responsibility.

Communication:
·         Provide communication forum for the exchange of ideas and information with the department.
·         Organize verbal and written ideas clearly and use an appropriate business style.
·         Ask questions; encourage input from team members.
·         Assess communication style of individual team members and adapt own communication style accordingly.

FUNCTIONAL MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES (if applicable)

Business Strategy and Direction:
·         Know and understand the campus strategic directions.
·         Define, develop and implement Failure Analysis Engineering strategies, which contribute to the campus strategic directions.
·         Provide regular updates to Test Engineering Manager on the execution of the strategy.

Cost Management:
·         Identify creative ways to reduce cost by streamlining processes and systems (i.e. modification of responsibilities or consolidation of tasks, elimination of non-value-added processes, or complete re-engineering of processes and systems).
·         Utilize tools to monitor departmental cost and cost trends, striving continuously to improve value.
·         Provide feedback to Test Engineering Manager on cost and cost trends.
·         May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.
JOB QUALIFICATIONS
KNOWLEDGE REQUIREMENTS

·         Ability to read, analyze, interpret and communicate regarding common scientific and/or technical journals, financial reports, and legal documents.
·         Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community.
·         Ability to effectively present information to top management, public groups, and/or boards of directors.
·         Advanced PC skills, including training and knowledge of Jabil’s software packages.
·         Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistics, statistical inference,  fundamentals of plane and solid geometry and trigonometry, understanding of partial differential equations, integration, and numerical techniques.
·         Expertise in applying concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.
·         Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists.
·         Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.
·         Ability to collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Proven ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and effectively deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

招聘岗位：FA高级工程师（Senior Failure Analysis Engineer）

一、岗位职责

• 负责产品失效分析（FA）工作，包括客户退货、可靠性测试失效、生产异常及品质问题分析。
• 独立完成失效样品拆解、检测、验证及分析报告编写。
• 推动异常问题关闭，与研发、质量、制造、供应商等跨部门团队合作落实纠正预防措施（CAPA）。
• 建立和优化失效分析流程、测试方法及相关SOP。
• 负责可靠性测试失效件分析，包括寿命测试、跌落测试、环境测试等。
• 熟悉手表或电子产品显示屏结构及Panel完整工作原理，精通像素驱动、背光原理、触控感应、电路导通、屏幕显示成像逻辑，了解Panel生产、切割、贴合、封装核心制程。

二、任职要求

教育背景

• 本科及以上学历；
• 材料工程、机械工程、电子工程、物理学等相关专业优先。

工作经验

• 5年以上失效分析（FA）、可靠性工程、品质工程相关工作经验；（熟练英语可放宽至3年）.
• 有消费电子、智能硬件、电子配件、结构件或金属产品行业经验优先；
• 具备独立主导复杂失效案件分析经验。

语言能力

• 英语读写说熟练；
• 能够与海外客户进行技术邮件沟通及会议汇报。

jobs.title: Full Time - Sales Associate - Paint - Day
jobs.description:
Your Impact at Lowe's

As a Customer Service Associate, you combine top-notch customer service skills with genuine care for people to help customers feel comfortable while shopping at Lowe's. This is an excellent role for those who want to engage with customers and help them solve their home improvement challenges.

How We Support You

Whether you need a part-time position or a place to plant yourself and grow, Lowe's is ready to support your goals. As a Lowe's associate, you'll gain access to many benefits beyond competitive pay and flexible schedules.

• Make your well-being a priority with multiple top-tier health insurance options.
• Explore educational opportunities with Lowe's tuition assistance program.
• Take charge of your financial future with a company-matching 401(k) and optional Employee Stock Purchase Program.
• Gain extra savings with a 10% Associate Discount.
• Learn new trade skills with our Track to the Trades program.

For information about our benefit programs and eligibility, please visit https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/benefits.

Your Day at Lowe's

As a Customer Service Associate, you will welcome customers to Lowe's and help them find the right products and services for their home improvement needs. You will interact with customers throughout the day, help them find and select products, occasionally load merchandise, and ensure all customer needs are met.

While you will spend most of your time listening to customers, answering questions, and organizing merchandise, your daily responsibilities may vary by department.

Customer Service Associates work in one of the following departments, based on hiring needs and skillsets: Appliances, Cabinets, Flooring, Live Nursery, Inside Garden, Hardware, Tools, Millwork, Building Materials, Plumbing, Electrical, Paint, Home Décor, Tool Rental, or Pro Services.

Key Responsibilities

• Welcome customers to Lowe's, answer questions, and deliver friendly and professional customer service.
• Assist customers with locating and handling merchandise
• Down stock merchandise by looking for empty areas on shelves and replenishing supplies
• Process orders and deliveries accurately so customers receive merchandise as expected and on time
• Cross-functionally train in other areas of the store to help deliver the best customer service
• Prepare merchandise in your department based on customer needs (e.g., tint and mix paint, cut and thread pipe, cut and bundle wood, cut drywall, cut blinds)
• Guide customers through shopping or checkout
• Complete other duties as assigned

Minimum Qualifications

• 6 Months Experience using a computer, including inputting, accessing, modifying, or outputting information
• 6 Months Experience using common retail technology, such as smart phones and tablets
• Reading, writing, and performing basic arithmetic (addition and subtraction)
• Able to perform duties that may require prolonged standing, sitting, and other activities necessary to perform job duties
• Minimally lift 25lbs unassisted or over 25lbs with or without an accommodation

Preferred Qualifications

• 6 months of Retail and/or customer service experience
• Bi-lingual skills
• Certification in trade related to department (e.g., hardware, kitchen, plumbing, electrical, lawn and garden, and lumber/building materials)

Lowe's commitment to growth and teamwork extends to the community as well. To better equip our stores and serve our communities, we strongly encourage bilingual, military, and veteran talent to apply and join our team.

Travel Requirements

This role does not require regular travel; however, this role may need to travel occasionally to meetings, training, or to support neighboring stores.

Working Conditions

Environmental factors vary by location. You may be working in both inside and outside weather conditions. Exposure to varying climates, including extreme heat or cold, wet, damp, humid, windy, or drafty conditions, is possible. You may be exposed to constant or intermittent noises in addition to moving or shaking objects and equipment.

Lifting methods vary based on role, weight, and volume. Associates must follow guidelines, limiting single lifts to 75 pounds. Team lifts are used minimally starting at 75 pounds or when needed. Powered equipment should be used as required, with proper training or assistance from a trained coworker.

jobs.title: Full Time - Head Cashier - Day
jobs.description:
Key Responsibilities

• Provides SMART customer service at all times through the daily execution of Lowe's customer service policies, procedures and programs

• Seeks out customers to understand his/her needs and assists in locating, demonstrating, selecting, carrying, and/or loading merchandise

• Listens to and responds knowledgeably and promptly to customer and employee questions by taking them to areas of the store and walking them through projects when necessary

• Communicates information to customers regarding all stock, special order merchandise, feature benefits, application, and warranty information related to Lowe’s programs

• Coaches, develops, provides feedback, and trains associates in the various departmental duties or sales opportunities (CSA Front End Team)

• Uses a cash register to process sales transactions, returns, and refunds according to company guidelines

• Provides proper monetary change to CSA Front End associates for register activities

• Removes security tags, verifies product information, and bags merchandise for customers

• Assists in line vesting to help turn around time for checkout, opening additional registers when necessary to ensure enough coverage

• Prepares register area at the beginning and end of shift by confirming functionality of registers and scanners and stocking register supplies

• Inspects returned merchandise for damages

• Enters and submits customer orders, prints order tickets, verifies receipts, and signs off on loading tickets

• Looks up product information and competitor prices for products to verify price match

• Records all items that are used in the store on the store use lists

• Completes cash counting and daily reconciliation duties as assigned

• Monitors cash in drawer and cash recycler levels to ensure they do not exceed limit requirements

• Monitors merchandise entering and leaving the store entrances and exits and assists customers or associates who trigger the alarm

• Detects common signs of shoplifting, theft, and other security risks, and promptly communicates them to management and/or Asset Protection

• Ensures compliance with housekeeping standards and programs (e.g., Zone Recovery) to maintain cleanliness and organization of store and working areas

• Maintains a safe and secure work environment, which may include conducting daily safety reviews, noting hazards, keeping aisles clear, and securing doors and gates

• Adheres to all safety requirements relevant to one’s regular job duties: top stock safety, reinstalling safety cables, use of aisle blockers, a tether line on power equipment, spotters, and safety devices

• Operates store equipment as needed depending on one specific role and department (e.g., Zebra phone, telephone, paging system, cash recycler, copiers, fax machines, computers, CCTV surveillance system, key cutter, panel saw, paint mixer, flooring cutters, compacter baler)

• In addition to the above responsibilities, this individual is held accountable for other duties as assigned

Required Qualifications

• High school diploma or GED or equivalent years of experience in lieu of education requirement, if applicable
• Less than 1 Year Experience using a computer, including inputting, accessing, modifying, or outputting information

• Less than 1 Year Experience using common retail technology, such as smart phones and tablets

• 1 Year Retail experience as a cashier
• Ability to obtain sales related licensure or registration as may be required by law

Preferred Qualifications

• 1 Year Experience identifying and selling products based on customer needs, including credit cards, installations, add-on sales, protection plans, and explaining warranties, product features, and benefits

jobs.title: Part Time - Receiver/Stocker - Flexible
jobs.description:
Your Impact at Lowe’s

As a Receiver/Stocker, you help keep the store clean, safe, and ready for customers by accurately receiving freight, stocking shelves, and organizing merchandise and top stock. You’ll unload deliveries, handle equipment and hazardous materials safely, and make sure your area is prepped for daily success.

This role is physical and fast-paced, requiring safe lifting practices and attention to detail. You’ll spend most of your shift on your feet, working mornings, afternoons, evenings, or overnight depending on store needs. And when a customer or teammate needs help, you’ll be there with a friendly, professional attitude.

How We Support You

Whether you need a part-time position or a place to plant yourself and grow, Lowe’s is ready to support your goals. As a Lowe’s associate, you’ll gain access to many benefits beyond competitive pay and flexible schedules.

• Make your well-being a priority with multiple top-tier health insurance options.
• Explore educational opportunities with Lowe’s tuition assistance program.
• Take charge of your financial future with a company-matching 401(k) and optional Employee Stock Purchase Program.
• Gain extra savings with a 10% Associate Discount.
• Learn new trade skills with our Track to the Trades program.

For information about our benefit programs and eligibility, please visit https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/benefits.

Your Day at Lowe’s

You’ll keep shelves stocked and backrooms organized by unloading freight, moving products to the sales floor, and maintaining a clean, safe workspace. You may also assist customers in locating or loading products. Most shifts are physically active, and scheduling may include morning, evening, or overnight hours based on store needs.

Key Responsibilities

• Deliver SMART customer service by assisting customers, answering questions, and offering support during projects
• Stock merchandise by unloading freight, down-stocking, organizing shelves, and setting up pallets
• Support store operations by verifying deliveries, completing dock prep, and using equipment like pallet jacks and forklifts
• Maintain a safe, clean environment by following proper procedures for hazardous materials, equipment use, and housekeeping
• Operate store equipment including scanners, Zebra phones, balers, and other tools as needed
• Pitch in as a team player to complete other assigned tasks

Additional responsibilities for Pro Fulfillment Stores include:

• Use the Orders App to pick and stage Flatbed Delivery orders
• Load delivery orders, ensuring quality, accuracy, and safe loading practices
• Rotate orders by delivery date and resolve customer order issues
• Proactively communicate with customers to ensure delivery satisfaction
• Execute Delivery Readiness best practices

Minimum Qualifications

• High school diploma or GED or equivalent years of experience in lieu of education requirement, if applicable

Preferred Qualifications

• 3 months Experience operating forklift/power equipment such as lifts, order pickers, and similar equipment
• 6 months Experience in a warehouse performing inventory handling and stocking

Lowe’s commitment to growth and teamwork extends to the community as well. To better equip our stores and serve our communities, we actively seek and encourage bilingual, military, and veteran talent to apply and join our team.

This role does not require regular travel, but occasional travel may be needed for meetings, training sessions, or to support nearby stores.

Environmental factors vary by location. You may be working in both inside and outside weather conditions. Exposure to varying climates, including extreme heat or cold, wet, damp, humid, windy, or drafty conditions, is possible. jobs.title: Early in Career Development Programme - Procurement 2027
jobs.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

Job title: Graduate Procurement Specialist

Location: Burgess Hill, Sussex, UK

Length of programme: 2 years (September 2027 - August 2029)

Finance & Operations Early Careers: Graduate Procurement Specialist opportunity

Our Early in Career Development Programme accelerates your growth to directly impact patients' lives. Start your career with a UK market leader in biotechnology, recognised as the #1 Best Big Company to Work For (2021) and dedicated to equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Job Purpose

At Roche Diagnostics, our mission is to improve patients’ lives through innovative diagnostic solutions. Procurement supports this mission by securing the suppliers, products and services needed by our business, colleagues and customers.

A rare opportunity has been made available in the procurement function in the UK &  Ireland team. The role is based in the Finance & Operations Directorate. The function ensures organisational efficiency and excellence through robust supply frameworks, optimised sourcing, and aligned strategic planning, foresight and execution.

As a Graduate Procurement Specialist, you will join a collaborative team and gain practical experience across strategic sourcing, supply chain resilience,  supplier management, commercial analysis, compliance and continuous improvement. Working with experienced professionals and stakeholders across Roche you will apply your commercially savvy mindset with academic knowledge while developing a career in procurement and supply chain management.

We are looking for someone commercially inclined with a keen eye for detail, curious, motivated and eager to learn who wants to develop as a procurement professional.

The role is a paid, full-time graduate role of two years’ duration, based in Burgess Hill, West Sussex with hybrid working with 3 days in office.

The Opportunity

You will gain exposure to the full procurement lifecycle, including:

• Support tenders, quotation analysis and commercial evaluations to secure value while maintaining quality, service and compliance.
• Monitor performance, maintain relationships and identify opportunities to improve service, resilience and value.
• Analyse procurement and supplier data to identify trends, risks, savings opportunities and actionable insights.
• Work with Finance, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain and other teams to understand requirements and support effective decisions.
• Assist with contract administration, purchasing compliance and adherence to Roche policies and relevant regulations.
• Help simplify processes, improve ways of working and use digital tools and data more effectively.
• Contribute to responsible sourcing, supplier sustainability and Roche’s environmental and social ambitions.
• Support procurement projects from requirements gathering through implementation, tracking progress and benefits.
• Support exploration of AI and automation opportunities within Procurement processes, including assessing the overall AI/automation landscape as well as the feasibility of AI/automation solutions.

As you develop, you will take greater ownership, contribute ideas and build confidence in making evidence-based commercial recommendations.

Why a Procurement programme at Roche?

Join a world-leading  innovative organisation. Experience a science-led international environment that values collaboration, learning and new ideas.

Grow your career. Grow in Global or affiliate procurement roles. Contribute to meaningful business challenges and build skills for a long-term career in procurement, supply chain or commercial management.

Build a strong commercial foundation. Develop experience across sourcing, supplier management, commercial analysis, contracts and procurement operations.

Turn data into value. Learn how procurement insights can improve decisions, manage risk, enhance performance and deliver sustainable value.

Who You Are

Essential Skills & Experience

We are seeking a graduate with initiative and an interest in how procurement creates value for businesses and customers.

Essential requirements

• A degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business, Finance, Economics, STEM or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant academic experience.
• Strong analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to interpret information and draw logical conclusions.
• Effective communication and interpersonal skills, including confidence engaging with colleagues and suppliers.
• Strong organisation, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities.
• A proactive, problem-solving approach and willingness to ask questions, challenge constructively and suggest improvements.
• A collaborative, accountable and ethical approach to working with others and following policies.
• Confidence using Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, or willingness to develop these skills.
• Genuine interest in procurement, commercial management, negotiations, sourcing, supplier relationships and healthcare or diagnostics.

What will help you succeed?

Extensive procurement experience is not required. We value enthusiasm, curiosity and willingness to learn alongside technical knowledge.

• Strong interest in commercial processes, compliance, problem-solving, or data governance within a regulated environment
• Experience or knowledge within automation / AI, metrics, dashboards, and performance frameworks (e.g., OKRs, KPIs)
• Comfortable with a continuous improvement mindset and challenging the “why” with a willingness to take ownership of tasks
• Comfortable working with ambiguity and eager to learn in a fast-paced environment
• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Experience creating presentations or working with data in PowerBI, Appsheets, Tableau or similar tools

You will thrive if you enjoy working with data, solving problems, understanding business operations and turning ideas into practical initiatives. Above all, you should be motivated to develop, take ownership and contribute to a shared purpose.

Application process:

Stage 1: Submit your CV and cover letter

• Our focus is to understand why you have applied for this role and what you will bring to the role to ensure team and personal success.
• Applications close on Friday, 16 October 2026. The application process may be extended beyond this date but could close at any point after this time.

Stage 2: Recorded video interview

• You will take part in a recorded video interview, where you wil be presented with questions and record your answer to support your application
• Estimated date: November 2026

Stage 3: In person assessment centre

• You will take part in our full day in person assessment centre at our Roche offices in Burgess Hill, Sussex. Further details will be provided if successful.
• Expected date: w/c 07 December 2026. The exact date will be provided if successful.

Please note: Unfortunately, visa sponsorship is not available for this role. Candidates must already hold a valid authorisation to work in the UK.

Ready to apply? Go ahead and join us, we are waiting for you!

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Furthermore, they do not establish a contract for employment and are subject to change at the discretion of Roche Products Ltd. At Roche Products we believe diversity drives innovation and we are committed to building a diverse and flexible working environment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion or belief, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, disability or age. We recognise the importance of flexible working and will review all applicants’ requests with care. At Roche difference is valued and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer where you are encouraged to bring your whole self to work.

jobs.title: Sprzedawca/Sprzedawczyni
jobs.description:
TK Maxx

At TJX Europe, every day brings new opportunities for growth, exploration, and achievement. You’ll be part of our vibrant team that embraces diversity, fosters collaboration, and prioritises your development. Whether you’re working in our Distribution Centers, Corporate Offices, or Retail Stores—TK Maxx & Homesense, you’ll find abundant opportunities to learn, thrive, and make an impact. Come join our TJX team—a Fortune 100 company and the world’s leading off-price retailer.

Job Description:

Sprzedawca/Sprzedawczyni

W TJX Europe każdy dzień przynosi nowe możliwości rozwoju, zdobywania wiedzy i odniesienia sukcesu. Będziesz częścią naszego energicznego zespołu, który stawia na różnorodność, współpracę i priorytetowo traktuje Twój rozwój. Niezależnie od tego, czy pracujesz w naszym centrum dystrybucyjnym, biurze czy sklepie TK Maxx lub Homesense, przed Tobą wiele możliwości do nauki, rozwoju i wywarcia pozytywnego wpływu. Dołącz do zespołu TJX – firmy, która znalazła się w rankingu „Fortune 100” i jest wiodącym sprzedawcą detalicznym działającym w modelu off-price na całym świecie.

Opis stanowiska:

TK Maxx jest częścią grupy TJX Europe, w której znajdziesz różne produkty, ale łączy nas ta sama cecha – poszukiwanie skarbów, które dają nam radość. Od stylowych perełek, znanych marek do unikatowej biżuterii, gwarantujemy naszym klientom szalone możliwości każdego dnia. Równie dynamiczna jest nasza praca. W sklepach nieustannie coś się dzieje, co sprzyja rozwojowi i zaangażowaniu. Każdy dzień daje możliwość odkrycia czegoś nowego.

Dołącz do naszego zespołu na stanowisku: Sprzedawcy/Sprzedawczyni

Zatrudnienie w pełnym/niepełnym wymiarze godzin

Stawka wynagrodzenia na tym stanowisku wynosi 30,34 zł brutto za godzinę.

Jest to jednolita stawka wynagrodzenia dla wszystkich pracowników sklepu w tej lokalizacji.

Szukasz pracy, dzięki której zajdziesz daleko?

Osoba na tym stanowisku reprezentuje naszą markę, dlatego powinna być pewna siebie i komunikatywna. Wyobraź sobie pracę, w której nie ma dwóch takich samych dni. W sklepach nieustannie coś się dzieje – w jednej chwili obsługujesz klienta, a za moment rozpakowujesz dostawę pełną nowych niesamowitych produktów.

Stając się częścią rodziny TK Maxx, dołączasz do zespołu świetnych ludzi – a to dopiero początek korzyści. Oferujemy szeroki pakiet benefitów wspierających zdrowie i dobre samopoczucie, w tym:

• Więcej urlopu na start
• Prywatną opiekę medyczną
• Ubezpieczenie na życie
• Dofinansowanie do karty MultiSport
• PPK
• Program nagród za staż pracy
• Zniżki pracownicze na zakupy w TK Maxx

Odkryj to, co nas wyróżnia w TK Maxx – przekonasz się, że to coś więcej niż praca. Jesteśmy dynamiczną organizacją, razem współpracujemy, uczymy się i rozwijamy. Dołączając do naszego zespołu w sklepach, możesz liczyć na pełne wsparcie różnorodnej i zgranej grupy.

Masz prawo wiedzieć, jakie informacje o Tobie posiadamy i w jaki sposób wykorzystujemy te informacje. W celu uzyskania bardziej szczegółowych informacji na temat wykorzystywania przez nas danych i praktyk ich udostępniania, prosimy odwiedzić: mytjx.com/mytjx/Global_TJX_Privacy_Notice.pdf i zapoznać się z naszą pełną Polityką Prywatności. W Spółce obowiązuje polityka ochrony sygnalistów.

*Jesteśmy pracodawcą równych szans. Ilekroć w niniejszym ogłoszeniu używa się męskich form gramatycznych, odnosi się to do wszystkich osób niezależnie od ich tożsamości płciowej. Zachęcamy do aplikowania wszystkie osoby, w szczególności bez względu na wiek, poziom sprawności, tożsamość płciową, stan cywilny, ciążę lub macierzyństwo, przynależność związkową, pochodzenie etniczne, narodowość, kolor skóry, religię, wyznanie, przekonania polityczne, orientację seksualną.

Share our determination to think bolder and bigger, and be part of our future. jobs.title: Assistant Store Manager
jobs.description:
HomeGoods

At TJX Companies, every day brings new opportunities for growth, exploration, and achievement. You’ll be part of our vibrant team that embraces diversity, fosters collaboration, and prioritizes your development. Whether you’re working in our four global Home Offices, Distribution Centers or Retail Stores—TJ Maxx, Marshalls, Homegoods, Homesense, Sierra, Winners, and TK Maxx, you’ll find abundant opportunities to learn, thrive, and make an impact. Come join our TJX family—a Fortune 100 company and the world’s leading off-price retailer.

Job Description:

We’re looking for an Assistant Store Manager who is passionate about fostering an inclusive and supportive environment. In this role, you’ll empower your team to deliver unforgettable “magical moments” for our customers. Every day will bring exciting new challenges and opportunities, keeping your work dynamic and rewarding. If you thrive in a fast-paced, ever-evolving environment, this could be the perfect opportunity for you!

Why Work With Us?

• We value integrity, respect, and teamwork, encouraging a unique and inclusive culture.
• Our comprehensive training and development programs provide you with the tools and resources to expand your skills.
• Enjoy Associate discounts at our stores, available to you and eligible family members.
• We have a range of global well-being programs focused on physical, financial, and emotional wellness.
• Exciting career paths with growth opportunities

What You’ll Do:

• Drive store performance by supporting sales results, managing expenses, and overseeing key operations including merchandising, backroom, frontline, cash office, customer service, markdowns, scheduling, shipping, and receiving, with a strong focus on minimizing shrink and damages.
• Attract, recruit, and cultivate top talent by providing comprehensive training and ongoing development for Associates. Serve as a mentor and role model, fostering a supportive environment that ensures a positive and engaging experience for both Associates and customers.
• Communicate and implement action plans for projects, targets, company initiatives, and store changes. Provide input on succession planning to meet future needs.
• Implement strategies to meet sales, expense, and customer service targets. Coordinate loss prevention and operational programs and improve store layout and efficiency.

About You:

• Minimum of 2 years of retail leadership experience as an Assistant or Store Manager.
• Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, and empower a large team.
• Excellent organizational and communication skills with ability to influence and provide effective feedback and mentorship to others.
