jobs.title: Director, Pharmacokinetics
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Pharmacokinetics, Dynamics, Metabolism and Bioanalytics (PDMB) function of our Research & Development Division, is seeking a dynamic and collaborative individual to lead a team of scientists in the Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics (DMPK) group in West Point, Pennsylvania.  The team primarily supports discovery programs across modalities (small molecules and conjugates) and therapeutic areas, enabling strategic decisions from lead selection through FIH.  As Director in the West Point DMPK group, your main responsibility is leading a motivated team of experienced Scientists representing the department in cross-functional teams as well as a group of bench scientists, charged with conducting mechanistic ADME studies. The position requires a focus on talent development as well as scientific creativity.

The DMPK director must be able to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment, drive innovation, and have excellent scientific, interpersonal and communication skills in order to guide the team on the design, implementation and interpretation of in silico, in vitro and in vivo studies necessary to influence decisions in drug discovery and development.

The ideal candidate will have an in-depth understanding of ADME, as well as pharmacokinetic and PK/PD principles that impact the discovery and development of new chemical entities. Experience with small molecules drug discovery is expected and additional experience with various drug modalities across therapeutic areas is desired. The candidate should be familiar with PK, PK/PD and PBPK modeling as tools to drive decision making.

We are highly engaged in influencing the success of a large and exciting portfolio and continue to evolve the influence of new computational and laboratory techniques towards the selection of differentiated products.  This role provides a unique opportunity to influence our evolving pipeline while enabling the growth of the next generation of leaders.

Education Minimum Requirement:

• PhD. in chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Pharmacology, Biomedical Engineering, Biochemistry, or related field with 8+ years of experience supporting drug discovery in the Pharmaceutical Industry.
• Applicants with MSci. degree with 12+ years relevant industry experience will be considered.

Required Experience and Skills:

• Experienced in providing DMPK support in drug discovery programs, including assessment of tractability, dose and PK predictions, drug metabolism, assessment of drug interaction risk and communicating analyses and recommendations to interdisciplinary teams and management.
• Experienced in integrating preclinical ADME, PK, and pharmacology data to enable translational PK/PD modeling and simulation to support dose selection, design of PK/PD and safety assessment studies, and dose justifications for preclinical and clinical studies
• Knowledge of cutting-edge in silico approaches to inform decision making related to the characterization of metabolism, drug interactions, exposure-response relationships and variability.
• Knowledge of modern instrumentation in support of DMPK workflows.
• Strong leadership, interpersonal, communication, problem solving, and collaboration skills along with strength in delivering results on firm deadlines.
• At least 3 years’ experience with management or supervision of staff.
• A strong aptitude for and previous experience in managing scientific teams and attracting, developing, and retaining talent.
• Excellent verbal and written communications skills and an ability to excel in a team-based environment.

Preferred Experience and Skills:

• Experience with authoring documents in support of regulatory filings, including IBs, INDs and CTDs as well as responses to regulatory questions.
• Experience with evaluation of third-party assets.
• Strong publication track record in ADME science and/or the Drug Discovery and Development field.

Primary Responsibilities:

• Providing strategic, scientific, and operational leadership for a group of scientists responsible for support, through experimentation and project representation on discovery teams.
• Actively working with staff to encourage and facilitate their career development.
• Collaborating with internal stakeholders to ensure the timely delivery of quality data and documentation.
• Collaborating with members of the DMPK organization and PDMB at large to support the advancement of scientific and strategic initiatives.
• Setting future strategy and facilitating/implementing new technologies in the organization
• Providing scientific oversight of programs supported by staff in the group and thorough and timely review of internal and external documents prepared by team members.

Required Skills:

ADME, ADME, Bioanalysis, Bioanalytical Assays, Clinical Pharmacology, Cross-Cultural Awareness, Dosing, Drug Development, Drug Discovery Research, Drug Metabolism, Drug Research, Immunoassays, Innovation, Investigational New Drug, In Vitro Research, In Vivo Studies, Mentoring Staff, Modeling Simulations, Pharmaceutical Analysis, Pharmaceutical Industry, Pharmaceutical Research, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Pharmacodynamics, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacology {+ 8 more}

jobs.title: Real Estate - Portfolio Management (Valuations), Associate
jobs.description:
Blackstone is the world’s largest alternative asset manager. Blackstone seeks to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies in which the firm invests. Blackstone’s over $1.3 trillion in assets under management include global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries and hedge funds. Further information is available at www.blackstone.com. Follow @blackstone on LinkedIn, X (Twitter), and Instagram.

Business Unit Overview:

Blackstone is a global leader in real estate investing. Blackstone’s real estate business was founded in 1991 and has US $314 billion of investor capital under management. Blackstone is the largest owner of commercial real estate globally, owning and operating assets across every major geography and sector, including logistics, data centers, residential, office and hospitality. Our opportunistic funds seek to acquire undermanaged, well-located assets across the world. Blackstone’s Core+ business invests in substantially stabilized real estate assets globally, through both institutional strategies and strategies tailored for income-focused individual investors including Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust, Inc. (BREIT). Blackstone Real Estate also operates one of the leading global real estate debt businesses, providing comprehensive financing solutions across the capital structure and risk spectrum, including management of Blackstone Mortgage Trust (NYSE: BXMT).

Job Title: Associate

Job Description:

This professional will be responsible for strategic support of the valuations effort and its related functions globally across Blackstone’s opportunistic and core+ strategies. The Associate will play a key role in Blackstone Real Estate’s valuations effort. This will involve a) coordination of the execution and outcomes of U.S. valuations, b) consolidation and analysis of global valuations outcomes, and c) execution of summary valuation-related materials and analysis. The role will involve partnership in coordinating key internal and external processes, consolidating and analyzing outcomes and metrics as well as delivering supporting documentation and materials to internal and external stakeholders. This professional will work closely with members asset management, finance, fund-specific and portfolio company teams to execute and enhance the overall valuation process and deliverables globally.

Responsibilities:

• Product and Investment Knowledge: Become proficient in Blackstone Real Estate’s global funds and investments, with particular focus on valuation practices.

• Valuation Outcomes and Assumptions: Work collaboratively across teams and vehicles to analyze and present valuation outcomes produced from a discounted cash flow approach by property, investment, market and/or sector, globally, to drive thematic monthly or quarterly valuation results.

• Valuations Process: Partner with asset management, finance and portfolio companies to coordinate and deliver monthly and / or quarterly internal valuations. Assist with the proper closure of key third-party processes, including appraisal, independent valuation advisor and audit.

• Internal Reporting: Oversee and execute quarterly valuation materials and supporting analysis to present results, requiring the aggregation and synthesis of large sets of data both internally and externally.
• Special Projects: Support global special projects relating to valuation strategies and process, new products, appraisals and third-party service providers.

Qualifications:

Blackstone seeks to hire individuals who are highly motivated, and have demonstrated excellence in prior endeavors. In addition to strong analytical and quantitative skills, the successful candidate should have:

• 2+ years; Strong technical background in valuations-related role (preferably in execution of DCF valuations)
• Experience executing files and presentations in fast moving and dynamic environment

• Inquisitive /critical thinker

• Collaborative approach, with confidence engaging directly with Asset Management and other stakeholders on behalf of the Valuations team to drive outcomes
• Strong organizational skills, with sound judgment in managing competing priorities
• Can take notes and distill to senior leaders in crisp and clear format
• Team player, excellent interpersonal skill

jobs.description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):

09

The Team

Americas Public Finance at S&P Global Ratings is an important sector of the capital markets, providing credit analysis that supports vital funding initiatives and serves as a growth driver for communities and economies across the region. The Local Governments Midwest Region team maintains a strong culture of analytical excellence and client service within a collaborative, diverse, and collegial environment that offers clear pathways for career advancement.

Responsibilities and Impact

Impact

This role is central to maintaining S&P Global Ratings' market relevance and meeting transaction requirements across the local government sector. The Rating Analyst leads credit analysis for cities, counties, school districts, special districts, and related entities — delivering independent, committee-ready credit opinions that inform investor decisions and support capital formation. This is a junior-level position with strong expectations and meaningful opportunity for upward mobility through demonstrated analytical performance.

Responsibilities

Core Analytical & Delivery

• Serve as primary analyst on credit transactions, conducting comprehensive financial statement analysis and preparing well-supported rating recommendations and committee-ready credit reports for local government issuers.
• Assess historical and projected financial data, evaluate fiscal health and credit risk factors, and compile findings into thorough committee presentations and effective written analysis.
• Publish timely, insightful credit reports and contribute to relevant research pieces and sector publications, staying current on developments in the municipal bond market.

Stakeholder & Market Engagement

• Serve as an active, voting member of rating committees, contributing to deliberations on rating outcomes and reviewing materials prior to publication.
• Meet with issuers, participate in investor calls alongside senior analysts, and communicate complex analytical perspectives clearly to diverse audiences.

Team Contribution & Capability Building

• Provide guidance and support to team members to maintain analytical quality and consistency across the portfolio.
• Contribute to team initiatives that improve processes, efficiency, and analytical workflows.

Compensation/Benefits Information (US Candidates)

S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $63,000 to $90,000 USD. Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual's geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses and certifications. In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan. This role is eligible to receive additional S&P Global benefits. For more information on the benefits we provide to our employees, please click here.

What We're Looking For

Required Skills and Experience:

• An S&P Global employee at this level would typically have 2+ years of relevant experience in public finance, local government finance, or a related credit analysis discipline.
• Demonstrated credit analysis and financial statement analysis skills, with the ability to assess fiscal health, creditworthiness, and key credit risk factors for local government issuers.
• Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information for diverse audiences, including committee presentations and published credit reports.
• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, deliver high-quality work under deadline pressure, and exercise sound analytical judgment under general guidance.
• Demonstrated ability to work effectively in team environments and independently when required.

Preferred or Helpful Experience:

• Experience advising on complex local government finance issues and providing analytical perspectives to senior stakeholders.
• Demonstrated ability to build and maintain professional relationships across teams and functions.
• Initiative in identifying problems and contributing to process improvement efforts.
• Willingness to adopt evolving analytical workflows, including AI-supported tools and processes.
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent required. A master's degree or professional certification (such as CFA) is highly valued. We welcome candidates from traditional finance disciplines as well as diverse academic backgrounds that support innovative and critical thinking.

Additional Information:

• We require all candidates who reach the final stage of our interview process to attend at least one in-person interview, which is ordinarily at your nearest S&P Global Ratings office. This must be completed before we can proceed to an offer.
• Employees are required to work from the office a minimum of two days per week.

Right to Work Requirements

This role is limited to persons with an indefinite right to work in the United States.

About S&P Global Ratings
At S&P Global Ratings, our analyst-driven credit ratings, research, and sustainable finance opinions provide critical insights that are essential to translating complexity into clarity so market participants can uncover opportunities and make decisions with conviction. By bringing transparency to the market through high-quality independent opinions on creditworthiness, we enable growth across a wide variety of organizations, including businesses, governments, and institutions.

S&P Global Ratings is a division of S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI).  S&P Global is the world’s foremost provider of credit ratings, benchmarks, analytics and workflow solutions in the global capital, commodity and automotive markets. With every one of our offerings, we help many of the world’s leading organizations navigate the economic landscape so they can plan for tomorrow, today.

For more information, visit www.spglobal.com/ratings

Advancing Essential Intelligence.

jobs.title: Principal Engineer, Security Architecture - DGX Cloud
jobs.description:
NVIDIA DGX Cloud is an AI Factory designed to power the next generation of AI and industrial-scale breakthroughs. As a Principal Engineer for Security Architecture, within our Security Engineering organization, you will own a core security domain of the AI factory: the architecture, the paved road that delivers it, and much of the code underneath. You will hold the security design bar across DGX Cloud from inside the teams doing the building, and this is a founding seat on a new team.

Security Engineering is a new organization at DGX Cloud, accountable for the security outcome of the platform, and Security Architecture is the function inside it that holds the design bar. Security here is fleet horizontal and stack vertical, so your work will cross every DGX Cloud engineering organization: you will embed with the teams building GPU clusters, control planes, and services, join their designs as a participant rather than an approver, and leave behind systems in which an entire class of risk is no longer possible. There is no architecture review board here and no approval queue. You are a senior IC with deep security domain knowledge, and the security bar holds because you helped set it and then helped ship it.

What You Will Be Doing:

• Own a Security Domain End to End: Take architectural ownership of a core domain of DGX Cloud security, from the design through the system running in production. That could be tenant and GPU workload isolation, workload identity, infrastructure and network, supply-chain provenance, hardened baselines and patching, or deploy-time policy and admission control.
• Embed with the Teams Building It: Join the design early, write the code, and help land it. The posture is not "you did this wrong." It is "here are the considerations we need to meet, I will help, let's go to work."
• Build Paved Roads, Not Gates: Engineer the secure path into the platform so that it is also the easy path. You are measured by whether teams take that path by default, not by the number of requirements you have written down.
• Engineer Classes of Risk Out of Existence: Finding a vulnerability is 4% of the work; building the system where it cannot happen again is the other 96%. When teams keep missing the same requirement, the paved road is wrong, and fixing the road is our job rather than theirs.
• Threat Model and Attack the Design: Run deep-dive threat models across the substrate, the orchestration layer, and the tenancy boundary, then go after your own designs offensively and feed what you find back into the baselines, the guardrails, and the detections.
• Carry the Bar into Execution: Turn the DGX Cloud security bar into reference architectures, requirements, and golden paths teams can build against. Raise gaps early, in the design, with the work to close them attached.
• Multi-Functional Collaboration: Partner with DGX Cloud platform, production engineering, and network security teams, and with NVIDIA's central security organization, to make the secure path real in CI/CD and in the hardware lifecycle. We operate horizontally across vertically organized teams, with influence rather than authority.

What We Need to See:

• Security and Infrastructure Engineering: Experience (typically 15+ years) across software engineering, SRE, infrastructure, and security engineering. You build systemic solutions rather than performing manual operations or "tool administration."
• Production-Grade Coding: A strong software engineering background with the ability to write clean, maintainable, and well-tested code. You should be comfortable building and operating production services at scale.
• Emerging Technology: You work with what is new rather than waiting for it to settle. Today that means writing and reviewing AI-generated code at the volume it now arrives, putting AI-assisted analysis to work in your own security engineering, and building for agents that act inside the systems you own. Tomorrow it will mean something else.
• Security Architecture in Practice: Designs you own that actually got built and run, in areas like multi-tenant isolation, identity and access, policy enforcement, vulnerability management, or detection engineering. You stayed on to operate them.
• Threat Modeling and System Design: Proven ability to build threat models for complex distributed systems, identify the architectural gaps rather than only the bugs, and engineer the solutions that close them.
• Distributed Systems and Linux Depth: Cloud-native architecture, container orchestration (Kubernetes), and hands-on Linux systems security including kernel-level primitives (eBPF, AppArmor, or SELinux).
• Influence Without Authority: Experience landing designs through teams you do not own, in environments where credibility and relationships, not org charts, determine whether the work ships.
• Foundation: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience) with 15+ yrs of relevant experience.

Ways To Stand Out from the Crowd:

• HPC/AI Security: Experience securing high-performance computing environments, RDMA-based networks, large GPU fleets, or GPU-specific security challenges.
• Cloud-Native Identity and Attestation: Expertise in workload identity frameworks (e.g., SPIFFE/SPIRE), hardware root of trust (TPM/HSM) integration, or confidential computing.
• Offensive Depth Turned Defensive: Real exploitation, red team, or security research experience that you have converted into engineering: the controls, guardrails, and detections that closed what you found for good.
• Open Source Impact: Notable contributions to security-focused open-source projects or a track record of engineering-focused security research. How have you represented and helped advance the industry?

NVIDIA is leading the way in groundbreaking developments in Artificial Intelligence, High-Performance Computing and Visualization. The GPU, our invention, serves as the visual cortex of modern computers and is at the heart of our products and services. Our work opens up new universes to explore, enables amazing creativity and discovery, and powers what were once science fiction inventions from artificial intelligence to autonomous cars. NVIDIA is looking for great people like you to help us accelerate the next wave of artificial intelligence.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Job Description

Job Description

Job Title: Machine Operator - Night Shift

Location: Topeka, KS (Mars Petcare)

Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

---

Mars is looking to hire a highly motivated Machine Operator for our state-of-the-art manufacturing plant in Topeka, Kansas.

Whether you are an experienced manufacturing professional, someone looking to transition into a technical field, or a military Veteran transitioning to the civilian workforce, Mars offers the structured training, tools, and supportive team environment you need to build a long-term, rewarding career.

As a day shift Machine Operator, you will become a system expert in your assigned production area. You will be responsible for the safe, efficient operation of advanced equipment, ensuring our products meet the high standards our consumers and pets deserve.

---

What We Offer (Benefits & Perks)

· Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance starting on day one.

· Financial Security: Competitive base pay, annual performance-based bonus potential, and a highly competitive 401(k) company match.

· Work-Life Balance: Immediately eligible (based on hire date) for up to three weeks of paid vacation, 12 Paid Holidays per year, and Sick Pay.

· Family Support: Paid Maternity & Parental Leave, Short-Term & Long-Term Disability.

· Career Growth: Access to world-class technical training, clear pathways for promotion, and educational assistance.

---

Key Responsibilities

· Equipment Operation: Safely and efficiently operate food-safe machinery and production lines to meet daily operational targets.

· Problem Solving & Troubleshooting: Assess equipment operating reliability and perform routine technical repairs, adjustments, and root-cause troubleshooting.

· Preventative Maintenance: Perform routine maintenance tasks and partner with the specialized Maintenance team on complex equipment upkeep.

· Quality Assurance: Execute critical food safety and quality checks (e.g., metal detection, inspecting date codes, monitoring dump logs) and maintain a high level of product ownership.

· Detailed Record Keeping: Keep highly accurate logs and digital shift support documentation using basic desktop and production tracking computer systems.

· Material Handling: Safely operate a forklift to manage material flow and inventory control principles in your production area.

---

What You’ll Bring (Qualifications)

Minimum Qualifications:

· Education: High School diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.

· Physical Capability: Ability to stand on concrete floors for extended periods, bend, stoop, twist, turn, reach, climb stairs, and lift up to 50 lbs.

· Safety Mindset: Willingness to wear proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including hair net, bump cap, ear plugs, safety shoes, and uniform.

· Certifications: Ability to obtain and maintain OSHA forklift certification (Mars will provide full on-site training and licensing).

Preferred Qualifications:

· Experience: 1+ years of manufacturing experience operating industrial machinery OR equivalent technical military experience (such as equipment maintenance, operations, or mechanical repairs).

· Technical Skills: Basic understanding of inventory control systems or experience utilizing enterprise asset management systems (e.g., SAP, GCSS, or equivalent databases).

---

Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide

At Mars, we highly value your military service. If you served in any of the following fields (or a related occupational specialty), your military training maps directly to the technical, safety, and leadership demands of this role:

· U.S. Army: Allied Trade Specialist (91E), Wheeled Vehicle Repairer (91B), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Horizontal Construction Engineer (12N).

· U.S. Navy: Machinist's Mate (MM), Machinery Repairman (MR), Engineman (EN), Equipment Operator (EO), Logistics Specialist (LS).

· U.S. Air Force: Aerospace Propulsion Specialist (2A6X1), Aircraft Metals Technology (2A7X1), Materiel Management (2S0X1), Pavements & Construction Equipment (3E2X1).

· U.S. Marine Corps: Machinist (2161), Metal Worker (1316), Engineer Equipment Operator (1345), Supply Chain/Logistics Specialist (3043), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531).

· U.S. Coast Guard: Machinery Technician (MK), Damage Controlman (DC), Storekeeper (SK).

About Mars, Incorporated

Mars is a family-owned business with more than a century of history making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. With almost $35 billion in sales, the company is a global business that produces some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, UNCLE BEN’S®, and COCOAVIA®. Mars also provides veterinary health services that include BANFIELD® Pet Hospitals, Blue Pearl®, VCA® and Pet Partners™.

The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom – inspire our more than 100,000 Associates to create value for all its partners and deliver growth they are proud of every day.

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Cisco IOS-XE (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
The application window is expected to close on: 10/29/2026

This role requires to be onsite in a hybrid model 4 times a week in our Milpitas office.

MEET THE TEAM

Our team serves as the engine of innovation, dedicated to building software that simplifies complex networking challenges through a user-centric, Design Thinking approach. We operate at the critical intersection of product management and engineering, ensuring our solutions provide seamless connectivity for a global customer base. Our group consists of high-performing, collaborative experts who thrive on transparency and a culture of continuous learning. We are most excited about pushing the boundaries of scale and velocity while directly shaping the future of Cisco’s software ecosystem. This high-impact environment offers a unique opportunity to influence both the architectural direction and the user experience of our most advanced networking platforms.

Welcome to the heart of Cisco’s enterprise networking innovation. We are the IOS-XE Image Install engineering team, a group of passionate systems software professionals dedicated to powering the infrastructure that connects the world.

OUR MISSION & IMPACT

In today's digital landscape, network downtime is simply not an option. Our team owns the critical Image Install component of Cisco IOS-XE, the operating system running across Cisco's industry-leading enterprise switching, routing, and wireless portfolios. We architect and deliver the software lifecycle management mechanisms that allow millions of enterprise devices to upgrade, provision, and recover seamlessly. From automated zero-touch provisioning to robust in-service software upgrades (ISSU), our code ensures mission-critical networks remain secure, resilient, and always online.

ENGINEERING EXCELLENCE & CULTURE

We operate at the intersection of deep systems programming and modern software engineering. Our work requires a rigorous understanding of Linux kernel mechanics, flash file systems, bootloaders, and high-availability architecture. We believe that true reliability begins with elegant design, rigorous automated testing, and a culture of continuous learning. As a team, we champion technical ownership, collaborative problem-solving, and a relentless drive for quality.

WHY JOIN US AS A SOFTWARE ENGINEER?

This is a unique opportunity to shape the foundational architecture of Cisco’s next-generation networking platforms. As a Software Engineer on our team, you will not just write code; you will architect robust, low-level systems that handle complex failure scenarios gracefully and scale to meet the demands of global enterprises. You will work alongside seasoned industry experts who are eager to mentor, collaborate, and push the boundaries of what is possible in network operating systems.

If you have a passion for low-level systems engineering, a commitment to reliability, and the drive to impact how the world communicates, we invite you to build your career with us at Cisco."

YOUR IMPACT

Design, develop, and maintain high-quality code by applying advanced C/C++ and Linux systems programming to solve complex networking challenges. Lead technical features from initial conception through production delivery to ensure our software remains robust, scalable, and secure. Drive the software development lifecycle by integrating Design Thinking principles to optimize system reliability and performance in high-availability environments. Mentor junior engineers and collaborate across functional teams to advocate for product innovation that creates long-term customer value. Identify technical risks early and conduct rigorous code reviews to maintain the integrity of our distributed systems and networking infrastructure.

"Drove innovation within the IOS-XE software packaging and installation pipeline, modernizing the software lifecycle management framework. Delivered highly modular and resilient upgrade solutions that scaled effortlessly across diverse enterprise routing, switching, IIOT, and wireless platforms, directly improving customer operational efficiency and network uptime."

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor’s degree plus 7 years of related experience, Master’s degree plus 4 years of related experience, or PhD plus 1 year of related experience.
• Application of C for memory management, concurrency, and multithreading.
• Experience with Linux systems programming, including POSIX IPC, sockets, and process lifecycle management.
• Experience in distributed system architecture, specifically control plane and data plane separation.
• Experience with debugging tools including GDB, Linux tracing utilities, and post-mortem crash analysis.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Demonstrated ability to lead medium-scale technical features from initial design to successful production deployment.
• Proven experience mentoring peers and junior engineers to foster technical growth and team excellence.
• Exceptional cross-functional communication skills, including technical writing, presentation, and stakeholder management.
• Experience with threat modeling and production monitoring to ensure system security and high availability.
• Ability to thrive in a collaborative environment and advocate for user-centric innovation using Design Thinking.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

Message to applicants applying to work in the U.S. and/or Canada:

The starting salary range posted for this position is $167,700.00 to $245,200.00 and reflects the projected salary range for new hires in this position in U.S. and/or Canada locations, not including incentive compensation*, equity, or benefits.

Individual pay is determined by the candidate's hiring location, market conditions, job-related skillset, experience, qualifications, education, certifications, and/or training. The full salary range for certain locations is listed below. For locations not listed below, the recruiter can share more details about compensation for the role in your location during the hiring process.

U.S. employees are offered benefits, subject to Cisco’s plan eligibility rules, which include medical, dental and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan with a Cisco matching contribution, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability coverage, and basic life insurance. Please see the Cisco careers site to discover more benefits and perks.  Employees may be eligible to receive grants of Cisco restricted stock units, which vest following continued employment with Cisco for defined periods of time.

U.S. employees are eligible for paid time away as described below, subject to Cisco’s policies:

• 10 paid holidays per full calendar year, plus 1 floating holiday for non-exempt employees
• 1 paid day off for employee’s birthday, paid year-end holiday shutdown, and 4 paid days off for personal wellness determined by Cisco
• Non-exempt employees** receive 16 days of paid vacation time per full calendar year, accrued at rate of 4.92 hours per pay period for full-time employees
• Exempt employees participate in Cisco’s flexible vacation time off program, which has no defined limit on how much vacation time eligible employees may use (subject to availability and some business limitations)
• 80 hours of sick time off provided on hire date and each January 1st thereafter, and up to 80 hours of unused sick time carried forward from one calendar year to the next
• Additional paid time away may be requested to deal with critical or emergency issues for family members
• Optional 10 paid days per full calendar year to volunteer

For non-sales roles, employees are also eligible to earn annual bonuses subject to Cisco’s policies.

Employees on sales plans earn performance-based incentive pay on top of their base salary, which is split between quota and non-quota components, subject to the applicable Cisco plan. For quota-based incentive pay, Cisco typically pays as follows:

• .75% of incentive target for each 1% of revenue attainment up to 50% of quota;
• 1.5% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 50% and 75%;
• 1% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 75% and 100%; and
• Once performance exceeds 100% attainment, incentive rates are at or above 1% for each 1% of attainment with no cap on incentive compensation.

For non-quota-based sales performance elements such as strategic sales objectives, Cisco may pay 0% up to 125% of target. Cisco sales plans do not have a minimum threshold of performance for sales incentive compensation to be paid.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Tech, Fulfilment by Amazon, Selling Partner Services
jobs.description:
Amazon's inventory identity system was built two decades ago for a simpler world — one product, one barcode, one country, one tracking number. That assumption now constrains some of the largest strategic bets Amazon is making: a global inventory pool that lets sellers stock once and sell everywhere, multi-box fulfillment for products like furniture and gym equipment  and a cross-border fulfillment network that treats inventory as truly fungible across regions.

We are looking for a Senior PMT to drive the vision for FBA Identity — a foundational transformation of how Amazon identifies, tracks, and fulfills physical products. You will own the product strategy and execution for globalizing inventory identity, decoupling barcodes from tracking numbers, and enabling a single product to be represented as multiple independently fulfillable units. This is not an incremental feature. It is a platform shift that touches 600+ downstream systems, requires sustained alignment across four engineering organizations (FBA, AFT, Catalog, SCOT), and directly unlocks billions in combined addressable opportunity across multiple programs.

You will work directly with Principal Engineers, Senior Principal Engineers, and VP-level leaders across Amazon's supply chain to define the architecture, run experiments in live fulfillment centers, and ship changes that compound across every program built on top of inventory identity. If you want to work on infrastructure that reshapes how Amazon's entire fulfillment network operates — and see your decisions show up in the experience of millions of sellers — this is the role.

Key job responsibilities
Own the product vision and roadmap for modernizing how Amazon identifies and tracks physical products across its global fulfillment network. Translate a multi-year platform transformation into concrete, shippable milestones that deliver incremental business value at each stage — unlocking new product categories, new geographies, and new fulfillment models along the way.

Drive cross-organization alignment across four engineering organizations that each own critical pieces of the architecture. You are the person who ensures they move together, resolves competing priorities, and keeps the program on track through a cross-org governance model with leadership.

Design guardrails, reversible rollout plans, and structured pilots that let us move fast without breaking the network.

Write the business case and technical requirements to quantify trade-offs across seller experience, fulfillment cost, and operational complexity, make recommendations, and present to leadership for investment decisions.

Shape the AI-accelerated execution strategy. This program leverages AI for discovery, deduplication, anomaly detection, and inference across complex product hierarchies. You will identify where AI compresses timelines and where human judgment remains essential.

Represent FBA in cross-VP goal-setting during OP planning. You will author the goal proposals, defend the investment asks, and ensure partner organizations formally commit resources.

A day in the life
You start with a design review alongside Principal Engineers, debating how a proposed change impacts fulfillment center tooling — and pushing back when a solution adds seller complexity.

Mid-morning, you review pilot results from two FC types, draft a remediation plan for newly discovered system dependencies, and escalate one issue to the relevant stakeholders.

After lunch, you present the quarterly roadmap to Directors and VPs, walking through sequencing trade-offs and landing a decision on what ships first.

You close the day writing a one-pager that translates a technical architecture choice into the business case leaders need to fund.

About the team
FBA powers commerce for millions of sellers and hundreds of millions of customers. The Identity team sits at the intersection of catalog, fulfillment, and supply chain — the layer that determines what a product is to Amazon's network, how it moves, and where it can be sold. Amazon's supply chain is evolving from regional networks into a single global system. Multi-box products, cross-border fulfillment, virtual multipacks, and inventory sharing all depend on a modernized identity layer. This team is building it. The decisions made here remove constraints that block billions in opportunity across the organization.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Global From Day1
jobs.description:
Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) is Amazon's service for worldwide sellers, offering access to Amazon's vast distribution network as a service. Sellers in 135 countries worldwide — from Fortune 50 companies to hundreds of thousands of small businesses and entrepreneurs — rely on our world-leading technology to grow and thrive across Amazon's marketplaces.

Global from Day 1 is a bold new program within FBA making it possible for sellers to reach customers worldwide — not someday, but immediately. Multi-country sellers earn 70% more revenue on average, yet only ~30% list in more than one country today. We're changing that.

We are building a marketplace-agnostic Global Inventory Pool at Amazon's scale — where sellers ship their product once and replenish seamlessly across all FBA regions worldwide. This means building the foundational systems that represent, track, and integrate inventory across Amazon's global fulfillment network in real time, at massive scale, connecting to every layer of the fulfillment stack — leveraging AI frontier technologies to give sellers and Amazon real-time intelligence over global inventory at a scale never done before.

Key job responsibilities
- Architect and build highly reliable, scalable, multi-tenant distributed systems that power Amazon's marketplace-agnostic Global Inventory Pool — designing services that represent, track, and integrate inventory across the global fulfillment network in real time, enabling sellers to ship once into GWD and seamlessly replenish across all FBA regions worldwide. Own the end-to-end design from the seller's experience through to every layer of the fulfillment stack, with low-latency, high-availability guarantees at massive scale.

- Drive engineering and operational excellence across the full software lifecycle — from design through implementation, testing, deployment, and operations — setting a high bar for software quality through code reviews, design reviews, and automated testing; improving CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, alarming, and incident response for mission-critical inventory systems.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Design, Operations, and Sellers to define and refine end-to-end inventory workflows, translating complex seller needs and business requirements into clean, maintainable, and well-tested system designs.

- Leverage AI and frontier technologies to build real-time intelligence capabilities over global inventory — enabling sellers and Amazon to make data-driven decisions on inventory placement, replenishment, and cross-border supply chain optimization at a scale never done before.

- Mentor and coach SDEs on the team — training teammates on how the team's distributed inventory systems are constructed, how they operate, how they integrate across the fulfillment stack, and how to produce high-quality, production-ready code through mechanisms like code reviews.

- Identify and resolve complex, ambiguous technical problems autonomously — proactively investigating system bottlenecks, proposing architectural improvements, and influencing technical direction within the team to ensure the Global Inventory Pool platform scales with Amazon's global growth.

Basic qualifications:
- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications:
- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Hands-on interest in applying LLMs and AI-native approaches to real engineering problems

jobs.title: Microbiology Lab Supervisor- Casa Grande, AZ
jobs.description:
Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Micro Supervisor is responsible for supervising the operation of the Plant Microbiology QA Laboratories, which is comprised of the following functions:  Environmental Monitoring Program, including equipment swabs, air samples, retort cooling water, ingredient water, and product samples; biochemical characterization and identification; raw material, in-process, and finished product testing; ensuring methods and procedures are appropriately followed; ensuring CAPA activities are followed through to completion; providing direction and technical expertise to Microbiology Laboratory personnel and to the plant; and providing leadership during problem solving situations related to microbial issues.

Working at Abbott

At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and your family, be your true self, and live a full life. You’ll also have access to:

•               Career development with an international company where you can grow the career you dream of.

•               Employees can qualify for free medical coverage in our Health Investment Plan (HIP) PPO medical plan in the next calendar year.

•               An excellent retirement savings plan with a high employer contribution

•               Tuition reimbursement, the Freedom 2 Save student debt program, and FreeU education benefit - an affordable and convenient path to getting a bachelor’s degree.

•               A company recognized as a great place to work in dozens of countries worldwide and named one of the most admired companies in the world by Fortune.

•               A company that is recognized as one of the best big companies to work for as well as the best place to work for diversity, working mothers, female executives, and scientists.

The Opportunity

This position works out of our Casa Grande, Arizona location in the Abbott Nutrition division. Our nutrition business develops science-based nutrition products for people of all ages, from helping babies and children grow to keeping adult bodies strong and active. Millions of people around the world count on our leading brands – including Similac®, PediaSure®, Pedialyte®, Ensure®, and Glucerna® – to help them get the nutrients they need to live their healthiest lives.

Casa Grande, AZ., is one of Abbott’s leading nutrition manufacturing plants in the U.S., reflecting our commitment to innovation and excellence. But we’re more than just a company, we’re a family. Working here you’ll be part of a family that works together to make a difference and enhance the lives of millions worldwide.

What You’ll Work On

• Responsible for implementing and maintaining the effectiveness of the quality system.
• Manages to ensure budgetary and staff requirements are properly met.
• Provides product and manufacturing microbial support for retort, powder, and aseptic lines.
• Interfaces with division personnel in the development of microbiological guidelines and specifications.
• Assures compliance to all procedures and policies concerning all areas of quality, regulatory, safety and human resources for all reporting departments.
• Coaches, develops, and mentors employees in areas of responsibility. Responsible for recruitment, selection, development and retention of employees. Conducts performance reviews; develops growth plans; interprets, implements and supports employee-related policies, procedures and programs. Assigns projects/tasks to direct staff.
• Develops and administers a technically sound Environmental Monitoring program, updating as appropriate.
• Leads problem solving efforts related to microbial issues.
• Directs plant initiated microbiological certification activities resulting from new or modified manufacturing facilities or processes.
• Interfaces with Division and Corporate QA, Manufacturing, Engineering, R&D, Regulatory Affairs and Purchasing to ensure timely completion of project activities.
• Provides technical guidance and support to plant.
• Assures lab test results reflect compliance to plant, division, and corporate guidelines and procedures.
• Assures test methods are followed.
• Attends plant Management Review meetings to communicate and oversee microbiological issues.

You’ll be accountable for meeting our compliance standards including FDA, OSHA and Abbott policies and procedures.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelors Degree in Food Science, Microbiology or related area.
• The position requires technical knowledge related to sterilization methods, microbial physiology, biochemical characterization of microbial isolates, disinfection/sanitization methods, and a strong understanding of aseptic handling procedures.

Preferred Qualifications

• Masters Degree in Food Science or Microbiology (preferred but not required)
• Two years experience in Microbiology testing methods and techniques plus two years Supervisory experience (preferred).

Shift

Night Shift – 6:00pm to 6:00am – rotating schedule, every other weekend off – training will be on day shift

jobs.title: Global Director, Accounting
jobs.description:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Allstate Protection Plans, formerly SquareTrade, helps customers protect the products they use every day, from phones and electronics to appliances and furniture.

We are seeking a Director of Global Accounting to lead accounting operations, financial reporting, controls, and transformation across our global business. This is an opportunity to shape how a growing, technology-enabled organization approaches accounting while building consistent practices across markets and legal entities.

The Director will combine strong technical accounting expertise with practical business judgment, global leadership, and a passion for modernization. A key focus will be responsibly applying AI, automation, and analytics to improve accounting quality, accelerate the close, strengthen controls, and create capacity for more strategic work.

What You’ll Do

• Lead global accounting operations and controllership activities across multiple legal entities and markets.
• Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual close processes, ensuring timely and accurate financial results.
• Maintain consistent application of U.S. GAAP, Allstate accounting policies, and applicable local requirements.
• Provide accounting leadership for new products, commercial partnerships, service contracts, revenue arrangements, claims liabilities, and market expansion.
• Strengthen balance-sheet governance, reconciliations, financial controls, and issue-resolution processes.
• Partner with internal and external auditors to maintain audit readiness and address findings.
• Collaborate with Finance, Tax, Treasury, Legal, Technology, Operations, Product, and other business partners.
• Develop and lead a high-performing global accounting team, including talent development and succession planning.
• Establish meaningful performance measures for close timeliness, accounting quality, control effectiveness, and operational efficiency.

Lead Accounting Modernization

• Develop a practical roadmap for using AI, automation, analytics, and process standardization across accounting.
• Identify opportunities to improve reconciliations, variance analysis, transaction classification, anomaly detection, accounting research, and close monitoring.
• Ensure AI-enabled accounting solutions include appropriate human judgment, documentation, data protection, and governance.
• Partner with Technology, Data, Risk, Internal Audit, and Information Security to implement responsible and sustainable solutions.
• Build AI fluency within the accounting team through education, experimentation, and adoption of approved tools.
• Measure transformation success through improvements in accuracy, close speed, controls, scalability, and employee capacity.

What You’ll Bring

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
• CPA, Chartered Accountant, or comparable professional qualification strongly preferred.
• Progressive leadership experience in accounting, controllership, financial reporting, or audit.
• Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, internal controls, balance-sheet governance, and close management.
• Experience supporting international operations, multiple legal entities, and global or regional accounting requirements.
• Experience leading accounting transformation, automation, ERP, or finance modernization initiatives.
• Practical understanding of AI, analytics, and emerging technology applications within accounting or finance.
• Experience in protection products, warranties, service contracts, insurance, consumer services, or another regulated industry is preferred.
• Public accounting experience with a major global accounting firm is preferred.

Leadership Capabilities

• Strong technical accounting judgment and financial integrity.
• Ability to lead across countries, cultures, and matrixed teams.
• Clear and credible communication with senior leaders and business partners.
• A practical, hands-on approach to solving complex accounting challenges.
• A track record of developing talent and building accountable, high-performing teams.
• Curiosity about emerging technology and a disciplined approach to responsible innovation.

Skills

Accounting, Business Acumen, Financial Accounting, Financial Statement Analysis, Performance Management (PM)

Compensation

Compensation
Compensation offered for this role is 190,000.00 - 250,000.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

***Total compensation for this role is comprised of several factors, including the base compensation outlined above, plus incentive pay (i.e. equity, bonus, etc.) as applicable for the role. ***

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Joining our team isn’t just a job — it’s an opportunity. One that takes your skills and pushes them to the next level. One that encourages you to challenge the status quo. One where you can shape the future of protection while supporting causes that mean the most to you. Joining our team means being part of something bigger – a winning team making a meaningful impact.

jobs.title: Global Process Engineering Authority – Stator Wind Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

The Global Process Engineering Authority (GPEA) will work closely with the Global Process Engineering Leader (GPEL) for the Generator Value Stream, the primary focus area will be developing and deploying global standards that improve the reliability, availability, and performance of GE Vernova’s manufacturing equipment and maintenance processes. They will analyze data, and work cross-functionally to implement proactive measures that improve generator processes.

In this role, you will also be responsible for cost reduction through standardization of equipment and processes, establishing standards, and ensuring adherence to these standards. You will also be a focal point for new technology introductions, asset transfers, new process introductions; inclusive of lead time, technology selection and recommendations for fixturing, process, control plans, and qualifications of manufacturing assets. The GPEA will coach and influence a dotted-line organization, comprised of factory technical leads across the supply chain. Critical to the role is leveraging analytical skills, the lean methodology and the guiding principle of creating process standards for equipment (“One Product One Process”) to drive SQDC in line with business and functional objectives.

The candidate chosen for this position will acquire strong technical knowledge and extensive exposure to manufacturing, engineering, quality, and safe process development. The selected candidate plays a key role in the value stream, and in building a culture of inclusion and respect for people as well as continuous improvement.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

• Define, control, communicate global processes for manufacturing assets, including facility integration, acceptance testing, machine health checks & calibrations, preventative maintenance plans, spare parts strategy, technical & technology training.

• Validate design specifications and shop floor application of new processes. Including EHS, Manufacturing Engineers, Engineering, Quality, Materials, Industrialization, Materials, and Sourcing.

• Develop and implement reliability improvement strategies using industry best practices such as FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), and Root Cause Analysis (RCA).

• Collaborate with maintenance, operations, engineering, and safety teams to design and implement preventive and predictive programs.

• Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) for equipment reliability, and track progress against targets.

• Drive continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing equipment downtime and improve quality processes.

• Lead investigations into failures and chronic issues, identifying root causes and implementing long-term solutions.

• Provide technical support for asset management, including equipment life cycle analysis and spare parts optimization.

• Participating in the design and installation of new equipment and implementation of processes, ensuring reliability is considered from the outset (Design for Reliability).

• Requires specialized knowledge within the function. Influence the development of strategy for the area of responsibility, including control of resources and influences policy formulation.

• Interprets internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes or services. Stays informed of industry trends that may inform work.

• Uses high level of judgment to make decisions and handle complex tasks or problems in areas of operational, product management, manufacturing, technology or engineering. Has ability to assess quality of information given and ask pertinent questions to stakeholders. Able to offer new solutions to problems outside of set parameters and can construct and provide recommendations. Uses multiple internal and some external sources outside of own function to help arrive at a decision.

• Will lead functional teams or projects with minimal resource requirements, risk, and/or complexity. Communicates difficult concepts and may influence others' options on particular topics. May guide others to consider a different point of view.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited university or college with a minimum of 10 years of industrial experience in manufacturing or quality OR a High School Diploma / GED with at least 15 years of industrial experience in manufacturing or quality
• 5 years of generator manufacturing experience

• Strong knowledge of engineering concepts and quality processes

• Ability to interpret blueprints, specifications, drawings, and schematics

• Project Management skills and experience
• Willing and able to travel approximately 25% globally

Technical Requirements

• Experience working cross functionally and Co-leading the implementation of manufacturing systems that support Next Generation Supply Chain migration globally across the Generator Value Stream

• Experience utilizing design for Six Sigma methodology (DFSS), including, measuring existing machine capability, analyzing process requirements, and developing a strategy to maintain / improve process yield

• Ability to deploy lean principles, including, Transformation Planning, 3P (Production Preparation Process), Total Productive Maintenance, Standard Work, Kaizen, Problem Solving, and Poka Yoke.

Desired Characteristics

• Managed a cost center or P&L with a solid understanding of operational metrics

• Direct leadership experience of both professional and production employees.

• Ability to coach and influence others and lead small teams

• Strong oral and written communication skills

• Strong interpersonal and leadership skills

• Lead initiatives of moderate scope and impact

• Ability to coordinate and manage several projects simultaneously

• Effective problem identification and solution skills

• Proven analytical and organizational ability

• Deep manufacturing technical expertise

• Has comprehensive knowledge of underlying principles, approaches, and methodology

GE Vernova employees rise to the challenge of building a world that works. In order to meet this mission, we provide varied, competitive benefits to help support our workforce: Our Culture | GE Vernova (gecareers.com)

Inclusion & Diversity

At GE Vernova, we believe in the value of your unique identity, background and experiences. We are committed to fostering an inclusive culture, where everyone feels empowered to do their best work because they feel accepted, respected and that they belong.  Click here to learn more: https://jobs.gecareers.com/vernova/global/en/i-d-e

Full time

Job Description:

The Opportunity

You will support the development and evolution of automation and digital solutions for power converter and grid-connected applications by working with product managers, sales, application engineering, customers, and cross-functional teams. The role involves gathering and structuring market requirements, supporting technology assessments, identifying gaps between current and future application needs, contributing to business cases and roadmap activities, and helping validate solutions against defined requirements. You will also support documentation, product improvements, technical change requests, and knowledge-sharing activities. By helping align product requirements with grid codes, operational technology cybersecurity requirements, data management regulations, and customer needs, you will contribute to reliable, compliant, and evolving solutions used in modern power systems, renewable energy applications, battery energy storage systems, and related grid automation environments.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Collect and structure market trends and customer requirements with product managers, sales, and application engineering.
• Ensure product solutions comply with grid codes, cybersecurity requirements, OT operational standards, and data management regulations.
• Work with key customers to discuss new developments and requirements.
• Support benchmarking activities for competitor solutions and emerging IT and OT technologies.
• Help assess gaps between current automation and digital solutions and future application needs.
• Develop business cases and studies to support closure of identified technology gaps and portfolio development.
• Contribute to validation activities by reviewing test plans, performance data, and compliance against requirements.
• Collaborate with R&D, sales and tendering, and operations while supporting training and knowledge sharing related to power converter applications.
• Responsible to ensure compliance with applicable external and internal regulations, procedures, and guidelines.

Your Background

• Candidate must already have work authorization that would permit them to work for Hitachi Energy in the United States.
• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in automation engineering, computer science, or a related field.
• Two to five years of relevant experience with power converters, inverters, electrical grid automation, system integration, or solution development within the renewable energy or battery energy storage sectors.
• Experience with power converters, inverters, electrical grid automation, system integration, or solution development within renewable energy or battery energy storage applications.
• Knowledge of power systems, low-, medium-, and high-voltage electrical equipment, and power generation equipment.
• Knowledge of programmable logic controllers (PLCs), industrial and electrical communication protocols, supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems, plant networking, control systems, plant automation, grid-code compliance, and OT cybersecurity.
• Fluency in English.

More About Us

You will gain exposure to cross-functional collaboration, product development activities, and evolving grid automation and digital technologies.

• Work on innovative energy technologies related to grid automation, power converters, renewable energy, and battery energy storage applications.
• Collaborate with experienced professionals across product management, R&D, sales, tendering, operations, and application engineering.
• Access learning and development opportunities through training, knowledge sharing, and product and system learning activities.
• Health and retirement benefits are available as part of the employee benefits program.
• Paid leave and flexibility programs are available in accordance with company policies and applicable programs.

• High school diploma or GED

jobs.title: Full Time - Receiver/Stocker - Day
jobs.description:
Your Impact at Lowe’s

As a Receiver/Stocker, you help keep the store clean, safe, and ready for customers by accurately receiving freight, stocking shelves, and organizing merchandise and top stock. You’ll unload deliveries, handle equipment and hazardous materials safely, and make sure your area is prepped for daily success.

This role is physical and fast-paced, requiring safe lifting practices and attention to detail. You’ll spend most of your shift on your feet, working mornings, afternoons, evenings, or overnight depending on store needs. And when a customer or teammate needs help, you’ll be there with a friendly, professional attitude.

How We Support You

Whether you need a part-time position or a place to plant yourself and grow, Lowe’s is ready to support your goals. As a Lowe’s associate, you’ll gain access to many benefits beyond competitive pay and flexible schedules.

• Make your well-being a priority with multiple top-tier health insurance options.
• Explore educational opportunities with Lowe’s tuition assistance program.
• Take charge of your financial future with a company-matching 401(k) and optional Employee Stock Purchase Program.

jobs.title: Venue Usher/Ticket Taker
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

Who Are We?

Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment and eCommerce company, comprised of four market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, Front Line Management Group and Live Nation Network.

As the largest producer of live music concerts, Live Nation Concerts operates over 45 venues across the United States.  For additional information, visit http://www.livenationentertainment.com/.

Who Are You?

Employees have a leading role in the service experience our guests have. The extent to which we recognize our employees for service well done, is the extent to which they will care not only for the guests, but for each other.

That’s why SAFETY for employees and guests is our first priority. We show CARE around every corner and look to create ENCORE moments of service excellence for everyone. And our commitment to EFFICIENCY, is our way of staying well-organized.

So, join us! We need these kinds of skills and talents as we Create Once in a Lifetime Experiences for our Fans.

The Role:

As an usher/ticket taker, you will help to ensure safety, engage with guests to assist with their needs before, during and after the show, and help to maintain the appearance, cleanliness & integrity of the venue during showtimes.

Job Functions

• Greet and welcome guests upon arrival.
• Scan and validate tickets at venue entrances.
• Direct guests to seating areas, restrooms, concessions, exits, and other venue locations.
• Verify tickets and credentials for access to designated seating areas and restricted areas as needed.
• Assist guests with questions, concerns, complaints, or other issues, escalating matters to supervisors or management when appropriate.
• Provide assistance to guests with accessibility needs, including expedited entry, manual screening, and guidance to accessible seating and other areas.
• Assist with maintaining a safe, clean, orderly, and welcoming environment for guests and staff.
• Monitor guest activity throughout events and address situations that may affect guest safety or the overall event experience.
• Assist with verifying staff, artist, tour, and other authorized credentials as needed.
• Assist with pre- and post-event setup and breakdown of equipment and guest service areas.
• Provide directions, instructions, and other assistance to guests both inside and outside the venue.
• Assist with emergency procedures, including directing guests to exits and providing instructions during evacuations or other emergency situations.
• Perform additional duties and responsibilities as assigned by management.

Qualifications

• Strong afternoon and evening availability on both weekdays and weekends is required.
• High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
• Previous guest service experience preferred; 1+ year preferred.
• Excellent attendance, punctuality, and time-management skills.
• Strong attention to detail and ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment.
• Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
• Sound judgment, tact, and diplomacy when interacting with guests, staff, tour personell and management.
• Ability to remain professional and composed in a variety of situations.
• Ability to stand and walk for extended periods, climb stairs, and occasionally sit, lift, and carry items weighing 25+ lbs.

Compensation:

• $20.00/hr
• Part-Time Employee Benefits Available

If the above description sounds like you and fits your background, apply online to join the Live Nation Entertainment team today at: https://www.livenationentertainment.com/careers/.

Applicants for employment in the U.S. must possess work authorization which does not require sponsorship by the employer for a visa.

Equal Employment Opportunity
Live Nation Entertainment strongly supports equal employment opportunity for all applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, pregnancy, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, marital status, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by state or federal law.

Hiring Practices
The preceding job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job.

Live Nation Entertainment recruitment policies are designed to place the most highly qualified persons available in a timely and efficient manner. $18.00 USD - $20.00 USD Hourly

jobs.location: San Juan, Puerto Rico, United States of America
jobs.description:
Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

This position is part of Medtronic's Diabetes business, focused on improving outcomes for people living with diabetes through innovative technologies, patient support, and access programs. The team partners across sales, reimbursement, customer support, and operational functions to help patients gain access to life-changing diabetes therapies and services.

Medtronic has announced its intention to separate the Diabetes business into a standalone company, subject to applicable legal and regulatory requirements. This planned separation is expected to create increased focus, investment, and agility within the Diabetes organization, supporting continued innovation and expanding the impact of our therapies, services, and solutions for patients worldwide.

This role is based in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and follows a Flex work model. During the onboarding period, regular on-site presence is expected to support training and integration with the team. The position supports patient access, billing operations, insurance verification, claims processing, and inside sales activities related to diabetes therapies.

The Inside Sales Representative, Patient Access, supports patient access, reimbursement, billing, and commercial activities related to diabetes therapies. This individual is responsible for processing billing transactions, validating insurance requirements, supporting benefit investigations, resolving reimbursement issues, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to help patients access and continue therapy. The role combines customer-facing interactions, operational execution, and commercial support within a highly regulated healthcare environment.

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:

• Process daily billing activities for diabetes equipment and supplies, ensuring accuracy and compliance with payer requirements
• Verify insurance authorizations, medical documentation, eligibility, and billing information prior to claim submission
• Resolve billing discrepancies, rejected claims, reimbursement issues, and revenue cycle exceptions
• Manage payer benefit verification and authorization processes to support patient access to therapy.
• Maintain current knowledge of payer coverage policies, reimbursement requirements, and authorization processes
• Collaborate with Sales, Reimbursement, Finance, and Customer Service teams to address access barriers and improve patient outcomes
• Support inside sales activities, including opportunity follow-up, patient retention efforts, and order coordination
• Prepare and maintain productivity, billing, reimbursement, and operational performance reports

Required Knowledge and Experience:

• Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of experience in inside sales, reimbursement, billing, customer support, healthcare operations, or related business functions

• Conversational English communication skills (minimum B2 level)

• Experience working with medical insurance plans, reimbursement processes, patient access programs, or healthcare-related services

• Experience supporting customers or patients through phone-based or remote interactions

• Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and business software applications

Preferred Qualifications:

• Knowledge of Assertus or similar reimbursement and patient access platforms
• Experience supporting diabetes therapies or durable medical equipment products
• Demonstrated ability to identify process improvement opportunities and drive operational efficiencies

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.
